It measures self-reported AI use and VARK preferences, not a quantitative learning outcome after an intervention. Exclusion under E3 (no comparison group without generative AI) is the first code that applies in protocol order; the design is also non-experimental, which would apply under the design criterion. Physical education is also not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of a failed criterion (no control group, correlational survey design).

title: Multimodal cyberbullying detection in Hinglish memes using a classroom framework based on large language models
rationale: The study is a classifier for cyberbullying detection in Hinglish memes using LLM-generated explanations and an mT5 model. It is not a learning activity with learners interacting with generative AI, and the content is social media moderation rather than STEM. Exclusion under E2 (content is not STEM) is the first code that clearly applies, since the domain fails regardless of intervention framing. No learner population or learning outcome is described.

title: Higher Mathematics Education and AI Prompt Patterns: Examples from Selected University Classes
rationale: The abstract describes students completing a questionnaire on engagement, perceived usefulness, and reflections on AI as a tutor, with comparisons between prior-experience groups. No quantitative learning outcome (achievement, knowledge, problem solving) is reported; outcomes appear limited to perceptions and satisfaction, which the protocol excludes. The two modules are compared by experience level, not against a non-generative-AI control, so comparison is also doubtful. Positive evidence of outcome failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified under E5.

title: Generative AI Use Patterns and Ethical Dilemmas among Pre-Service Teachers
rationale: Qualitative exploratory study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on the basis of a qualitative, non-comparative design; code assigned is E6 as the closest fit, though E3 (no comparison group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) also apply.

title: Chatgpt, Grammarly, and Quillbot: Perceptions of Students and Teachers towards the Use of AI Tools in Writing
rationale: The study concerns academic writing with ChatGPT, Grammarly and Quillbot, and English-education students. Writing is not a STEM domain, so E2 applies. It is also a descriptive survey and interview study with perception outcomes only, with no control group and no quantitative learning measure, so it would fail E3, E5 and the design criterion as well. Under the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E1 is not clearly triggered (the tools are generative), so E2 is the first code that clearly applies.

title: Structured Development of Learning and Assessment Tasks to Prevent Generative AI Misuse and Enhance AI Literacy in the Faculty in Physiotherapy Education
rationale: The abstract describes a faculty-wide curriculum development initiative with a descriptive student survey of GAI usage and perceptions. There is no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the study is a descriptive/implementation report rather than an empirical comparative study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense). The domain is also physiotherapy, which is health professions education and would fail the STEM criterion, but the first applicable code in order is E1/E2 considerations; since the intervention is faculty-facing curriculum redesign rather than learner-facing GAI, E1 would apply first. Note: E1 is the first code in order that applies (AI is used for curriculum design, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity with a comparison), so the correct code is E1 rather than E6.

title: Cultivating Responsible AI Use through Formative Assessment: Insights from ODeL Mathematics Students
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive study with frequency data from a questionnaire. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is applied as the first failing criterion in order. Note that E5 or E6 could also be argued; E3 is reported as the first in the protocol's listed order that clearly applies.

rationale: Cross-sectional survey study of perceptions and adoption intentions (TAM/SDT constructs) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Outcomes are perceptions and self-reported use, which the protocol excludes. Design is survey, which is excluded. Exclusion code E5 applies as the first failing criterion in the ordered list reached for this record; the design also fails (survey), but the abstract gives clear positive evidence of no learning outcome.

rationale: Descriptive proof-of-concept cross-sectional study evaluating generative AI outputs (learning outcomes, test items, standard-setting) for educators. Using the first applicable code in order, E1 applies since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence as Image Creation Support in STEAM Projects for Initial Teacher Training
rationale: The abstract describes a teaching innovation experience analysed through student portfolios and representative examples. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense). The abstract alone does not provide a quantitative outcome, which points to E5, but E6 is the earlier applicable code for a qualitative, descriptive experience report. Full text could be checked if the researcher prefers E5.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Physics Education: Transforming Learning from Primary to University Level
rationale: The abstract is a narrative overview of AI in physics education (discussion of challenges, policy, and future directions). It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in the order the protocol lists after E1-E5 would be considered; E1 and E3 to E5 are also not supported by positive evidence, so E6 is the best-fitting single code.

title: Generative AI in higher education: the roles of knowledge, willingness, concerns, gamification and digital literacy in shaping perceived learning effectiveness and academic performance
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey-based structural equation model of students' knowledge, willingness, and concerns about generative AI. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Outcomes are perceived learning and self-reported academic performance, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion is at the abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group and a survey design; E3 is the first applicable code in the order given.

title: From Inquiry to Simulation: Leveraging ChatGPT and Chatbots for Dilemma-Based Learning in Healthcare Education
rationale: The title places the study in healthcare education, which the protocol excludes as a health professions domain (E2 is the content code used for non-STEM content). The human comparison is a historical cohort of MSc students answering the same questions, not a control group of learners using a non-genAI condition, and the design is a benchmarking study rather than an experiment. E1 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Use Among Medical Students: Learner Perspectives for Clinical Educators
rationale: Cross-sectional online survey with descriptive statistics only; no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome (outcomes are AI use, usefulness, confidence, concerns). Not an empirical trial meeting the design criterion; coded E6 as a non-experimental survey study (first applicable code in order would be E1 only if intervention were clearly not learner-facing GenAI, which is unclear here, so E6 is the most direct failure). Medical education is also a health-professions context, which further argues against eligibility.

rationale: Abstract describes a classroom action research study with a single cohort of 40 senior secondary students (physical computing with micro:bit). It reports survey percentages and thematic analysis, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Single-group design with no comparison means E3 applies. Intervention is physical computing; the abstract does not describe learners using a generative AI tool as part of the activity, so E1 could also be argued, but the comparison failure is the clearest positive evidence. Outcomes are largely perceptions. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of no control group.

rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/analytical article that reviews international experience and discusses opportunities and challenges. Although the abstract mentions determining impact on pupils' learning outcomes, this is framed as a review of others' experience rather than an original experiment, and no comparison group or effect data are described.

title: Bridging technology and education: The use of ChatGPT in grading pharmacy student exams
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT-5) is used to grade pharmacy student exams; students do not interact with it as part of a learning activity. This is not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies (AI used only for grading / by faculty). No control group without generative AI is evident either (all conditions use ChatGPT grading vs human gold standard), but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

title: Graduate Students’ Use and Perceptions of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in Higher Education
rationale: No abstract is available in the index. Because the record is exclusion-worthy on positive evidence (perception-focused, health-professions venue), I exclude at the abstract stage with E2 as the first applicable code in order. Note that E2 is applied on the venue and title; the abstract is missing, so this is a judgement from limited information and could be revisited if the full text shows a STEM-content controlled experiment.

Design is also a survey, which would fail the design criterion; the first applicable code in protocol order is E5 given the abstract evidence, though E3 (no control group) and E6 (non-empirical is not applicable since it is empirical) also apply to the design. Abstract stage: exclusion is justified by positive evidence that the outcome is perception-based and the design is a survey.

The abstract gives no randomized or controlled design; the text is an essay describing applications, and the domain alone is sufficient for exclusion.

rationale: Abstract describes a convergent mixed-methods study with a single group of 200 SHS students surveyed after an eight-week AI-supported intervention; no control group is mentioned and the analysis is a correlation between exposure and perceived effectiveness (rho = .055). Perceived-effectiveness Likert measures are perceptions, not a quantitative learning outcome, and no SMD is computable. Positive evidence of missing comparison group, so excluded at E3 (first applicable code in order would be E3 given the design lacks a comparison group; E5 also likely applies).

title: Exploring the Application of Large Language Models in Instrumentation and Control Engineering Education: A Questionnaire Survey and Examination Performance Analysis
rationale: Abstract describes a questionnaire survey of student LLM usage plus an evaluation of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 accuracy on 342 exam questions. No learner-facing intervention with a separate non-generative-AI control group is described; the comparison is between two generative AI models, and the survey design is not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design. Positive evidence of failing comparison and design criteria supports exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that E6 (not an empirical study) would not apply since the study is empirical; the survey and model benchmarking do not meet the protocol's design requirement.

title: Using LLM to Identify Pillars of the Mind Within Physics Learning Materials
rationale: Abstract describes LLMs (GPT-4o, o4-mini, MAXQDA AI Assist) used by researchers to analyze physics textbook material for Five Pillars of the Mind, comparing LLM output to authors' manual analysis. No learner interacts with a generative AI tool, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is no control group and no learning outcome measured; the design is a case study of model accuracy. Exclusion under E1 as the first applicable code in order.

title: English Partnering Efl Students With Chatgpt To Enhance Students’ Skills In Oral Communication
rationale: Abstract studies ChatGPT for English as a foreign language oral communication, which is non-STEM content (language learning), so the Domain criterion fails. Also no control group is described and the design is unclear, but the first applicable code in order is E2 ... note that E1 and E3 are not positively evidenced at abstract stage. Language learning is explicitly excluded by the protocol.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Use in Dental Post‐Graduate Students: A Mixed Methodology Study
rationale: Cross-sectional mixed-methods survey with focus groups; no control group and no comparison of learning outcomes. Dental postgraduate education is health professions education, which is also outside the STEM domain. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's listing, since there is no control group without generative AI. The abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group, so exclusion is appropriate at abstract stage.

title: Adoption of Generative AI Tools In Higher Education: The Role of Attitude, Subjective Norms, and Perceived Behavioural Control
rationale: The record is a survey-based study of undergraduates' intention to use generative AI tools, using PLS-SEM on questionnaire data. It has no control group and no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, and it reports no learning outcome, only behavioural intention and attitudes. Under the protocol's code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is arguably not the first failing criterion because the tools are learner-used generative AI; E3 (no control group) is the first clear failure. Design is also not an experiment, and the outcome is affective/intention-based. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that the comparison and design criteria fail.

title: The evolving role of programming and LLMs in the development of self-driving laboratories
rationale: Abstract describes a hardware instrument (Claude-Light) with a REST API and photometer, plus discussion of LLM roles in lab automation. It reports no comparison group, no learner outcome data, and no experimental design; it reads as a device/perspective paper rather than an empirical controlled study. Exclude as not an empirical study (E6). Note the abstract gives no positive evidence of a controlled comparison, so this is a judgment on the design described; a full-text check could revisit it if the paper contains a controlled student study.

title: Student conceptions of generative artificial intelligence in early adolescence
rationale: The study is a qualitative focus-group analysis (critical discourse analysis, concordance and thematic analysis) of student conceptions of GenAI. It has no control group and no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is not experimental. Exclusion is on the comparison criterion (no control group without GenAI), which is the first applicable code given the protocol's order at the abstract stage; the design and outcome also fail, which is positive evidence against eligibility. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract. Population (Grades 7-8) is met.

title: Exploring the Impact of ChatGPT on Chinese Students’ Foreign Language Anxiety in Macau’s EMI Higher Education
rationale: The study concerns ChatGPT and foreign language anxiety in English-medium instruction programs, which is language learning and not STEM content (E2). It is also a correlational/regression study on acceptance and use with no control group and no learning outcome measure (E3/E5), but the first applicable code in order is E2. The abstract gives positive evidence that the domain is non-STEM, so exclusion is justified at abstract stage.

title: Designing Additional Professional Education Programs for Teachers to Develop Self-Regulation Among Primary School Students with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
Role of Large Language Model—Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Communication Skills in Undergraduate Oral Healthcare Students
rationale: The intervention is an LLM-based platform for communication skills training in dental students. Dentistry/oral healthcare communication about patient behaviour change is not a STEM domain under the protocol (health professions education is excluded). Other criteria are unclear, since the abstract describes a planned comparison with actor-led tutorials and only pilot feedback. Exclusion on domain (E2) is the first failing criterion in order. Note: E2 is applied on positive evidence that content is health professions/non-STEM communication training, and the protocol explicitly excludes health professions education.

title: LECTURERS PERCEPTION OF THE USE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE TEACHING OF SCIENCE EDUCATION IN NIGERIA
rationale: Survey of science education lecturers' perceptions of generative AI. Not an intervention with learners (E1 would also apply, since the participants are lecturers, not learners), and there is no control group or learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 on intervention, but the study's design is a descriptive survey, which is clearly an empirical study. Applying the protocol's code order strictly, the first failing code is E1 because learners do not interact with a GAI tool as part of a learning activity. Reporting E1 as the first applicable code.

title: Integrating reflection and annotation into writing tasks for science undergraduates
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/rationale paper that proposes approaches to modify writing assessment tasks. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Generative AI is discussed only as an assessment challenge, not as a learner-facing intervention.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Introductory Programming Education at Universities: Content, Assignments, Assessment
rationale: The abstract reads as a review/overview of teaching programming and how GenAI could be used ("This paper briefly outlines", "The following themes are reviewed"). It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion is supported by the description of the paper as a review of themes rather than a study with data. The design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment on this evidence.

title: Impact of generative AI on higher order thinking skills (HOTS) in higher education: a multi-actor analysis
rationale: The study relies on perceived influence of GenAI on higher order thinking skills, gathered through interviews, focus groups and a student survey. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions. Design is qualitative/survey-based, not an experiment. Exclude at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), which is the first applicable code in the order given; the abstract also lacks any comparison group, so E3 would also apply, but E5 is listed first in the reporting sequence as the primary failure on outcome. Note: strictly E3 precedes E5 in the code list only if ordering is by code number; by the protocol order E3 comes before E5, so E3 is the first applicable code. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so the correct code is E3.

title: Usability and Efficacy of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots (ChatGPT) for Health Sciences Students: Protocol for a Crossover Randomized Controlled Trial
rationale: This is a JMIR Research Protocol describing a planned trial, not an empirical study with results. No outcome data exist yet, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Health sciences students with a chronic-disease focus also raise a domain concern (health professions education is excluded), but E6 is the first applicable code in order. Abstract-stage evidence supports E6 directly.

title: Programming Assessment in E-Learning through Rule-Based Automatic Question Generation with Large Language Models
rationale: The abstract describes an LLM-based system that generates assessment questions, which is used by educators to produce evaluation items; the learner-facing generative AI intervention is not evident (this could be E1). It also reports a single group of 32 vocational students tested on the instrument, with no control group and no comparison, so E3 applies. Design is a validation/instrument study with no comparison group. Excluding on E3 at abstract stage based on positive evidence of no control group; the abstract does not describe any comparison condition.

title: A New Era of Learning: Considerations for ChatGPT as a Tool to Enhance Statistics and Data Science Education
rationale: The record is a discussion/commentary article ("This article focuses on the potential of ChatGPT... providing examples... suggestions") with no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies as the first failing code (E1 is not clearly failed on the abstract alone, but E6 is the decisive reason).

title: Evaluation of primary school teachers’ use and perceptions of artificial intelligence in primary school mathematics instruction: a mixed-methods study
rationale: The study surveys 302 in-service primary school teachers about their perceptions and self-reported use of AI in mathematics instruction. There is no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; the only outcome is perception. Perceptions-only outcomes fail E5. Population also fails (in-service teachers, not students), and the design is a survey/mixed-methods perception study with no comparison group. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 would be the first code to check, but the abstract does not clearly show learner interaction; the decisive reason is the absence of a learning outcome (E5). Exclusion is justified on positive evidence from the abstract.

title: The impact of an AI-focused ethics education program on nursing students’ ethical awareness, moral sensitivity, attitudes, and generative AI adoption intention: a quasi-experimental study
rationale: The study evaluates an AI ethics education program for nursing students measuring ethical awareness, moral sensitivity, attitudes, and adoption intention. The content is nursing ethics, which is health professions education and not STEM, so E2 applies. The abstract also does not show learners interacting with a generative AI tool as part of the learning activity, and no learning-outcome measure of STEM content is evident. E2 is the first applicable code in order of check among those clearly failing; E1 is not positively excluded at abstract stage, so E2 is reported.

title: Exploring Students’ Perception of Using ChatGPT in Higher Education
Generative AI-first Maths Support at a Regional Australian University
rationale: Abstract describes a GenAI agent trial for maths support for nursing and education students, which fits intervention, population, and domain. However, the abstract reports usage patterns (out-of-hours access) and qualitative conversation data, with no quantitative learning outcome or control group described. The abstract gives positive evidence of no quantitative learning outcome, so exclude at abstract stage under E5. Note that the abstract is the only information available; if the full text reports a controlled comparison with learning measures, it could be reconsidered at full text.

title: Nursing Students' Early Attitudes Towards the Use of Artificial Intelligence and ChatGPT: An Exploratory Study
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of nursing students' attitudes (GAAIS) with no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Positive evidence fails several criteria. Nursing is also health professions education, which is outside the STEM domain. Coded E6 as a non-empirical-intervention survey design; the first applicable code in order would be E1 (no learner-facing generative AI intervention), so E1 is the more precise first-applicable code.

title: Development and Validation of a Scale for Assessing the Effectiveness of Generative AI-Enhanced English Writing Learning Among Chinese University Students
rationale: Psychometric scale development and validation study (EFA, reliability) using a single survey administration to 282 students. It is not an empirical comparison study with a control group, so there is no experimental design or comparison. Domain is English writing, which is non-STEM (E2 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E1/E2/E3/E6; the study is not an empirical intervention evaluation, so E6 is the most fitting code. Note the protocol order places E1 first; the abstract gives no evidence of a learner-facing generative AI intervention being tested, but it does not clearly show E1 either. E6 is chosen as the best-supported exclusion because the record is an instrument-development survey study rather than an empirical intervention study.

title: Evaluation of the performance of four different large language models (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Copilot, and Gemini) in answering oral, and maxillofacial radiology questions: pilot study
rationale: The study compares four large language models with each other on multiple-choice questions posed to dental students. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The LLMs answer questions as a model accuracy evaluation rather than as learners interacting with the tool, but the decisive exclusion is the missing non-generative-AI comparison. The record is excluded at the abstract stage on positive evidence that the comparison is between generative AI variants only.

title: Teaching and Learning about Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Secondary Education Chemistry Classes
rationale: Abstract describes a mixed-methods study with pre/post measures of prior knowledge and student questionnaires in intervention samples, with no mention of a separate control group without generative AI. This suggests a single-group pre-post design (E3). The intervention is teaching about AI in chemistry rather than learner interaction with a generative AI tool, which is also doubtful. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of no control group in the abstract.

title: The pedagogical potential of generative artificial intelligence in the formation of linguo-mathematical competence
rationale: The study compares outputs of three generative AI models with expert content assessment. There is no control group without generative AI, and no learner-level quantitative learning outcome is reported; the design is not an experiment. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that clearly fails, since it compares only generative AI variants. Note that E1 could arguably also apply, since the AI is used to generate teacher materials rather than learner-facing interaction, but E3 is the clear positive failure. Also, no learning outcome measured in learners is described (E5 would also apply). Because the comparison is between only generative AI variants with no non-AI group, E3 is assigned.

title: Developing the educational performance of learning disabilities teachers in primary schools: ChatGPT program as a model
rationale: The study is a survey and interview study of teachers' views on awareness, usage, and challenges. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome for students, and no experimental design. It is not an empirical intervention study meeting the protocol, so it fails on design, comparison, and outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the first clearly failing criterion in a survey/perception study; this is a judgment that the study is a perception survey rather than an eligible empirical comparison. Population is teachers, which is not a student sample, so E4 could also apply. Stage is abstract, so exclusion is based on positive evidence that the design and outcome fail.

title: A Study on Poetry Writing using ChatGPT: Focusing on user perception and educational approaches
rationale: The study concerns Korean language poetry writing classes, which is non-STEM content, so it fails the domain criterion (E2). This is the first applicable code in order (E1 does not apply: ChatGPT use by learners is described). The abstract also reports mainly satisfaction and descriptive survey data, with no clear quantitative learning outcome or clearly described control group, but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion.

title: Enhancing Programming Education using GPT-Based Code Review and Automatic Comment Generation
rationale: Abstract describes a GPT-4o code review system evaluated with BERT-Score semantic similarity against reference comments, not a learning outcome measured in learners. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also appears non-experimental (E3/E6 possible), but E5 is the first applicable code in order given the abstract. Note: under the protocol order, E1 does not apply since the tool is learner-facing generative AI, and E2 does not apply since programming is STEM.

title: Immersive Virtual Learning Experiences of Senior Secondary School Students from India and Russia: A Mixed Method Study
rationale: The intervention is immersive VR (stand-alone head-mounted VR), with no indication that learners interact with a generative AI tool. The abstract only mentions generative AI as a future study direction. Also, the outcomes are experience and attitude scales (affective/perception measures), with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group described. E1 applies first as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

title: Reasoning under uncertainty in graduate health education: a scaffolded framework using large language models
rationale: The record is a Hypothesis and Theory article proposing a conceptual pedagogical framework. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Its domain is health sciences education, which is also outside the STEM scope (E2), but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.

title: Efficacy and limitations of ChatGPT as a biostatistical problem-solving tool in medical education in Serbia: a descriptive study
rationale: The study is a descriptive evaluation of ChatGPT's performance on 10 biostatistics problems from a handbook. ChatGPT was tested directly as a standalone tool; there is no learner group and no control group without generative AI. The design is not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order. The abstract does not give positive evidence of an E1 or E2 failure, so E3 is the cleanest code, though the design is also descriptive rather than experimental.

title: PROMPTING DIFFERENCE: COLLEGE STUDENTS WITH ADHD AND THEIR USE OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN LEARNING CONTEXTS
rationale: Qualitative honors thesis using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. No experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The record lacks any quantitative learning measure, so E5 applies (the design also fails the comparison and design criteria, but the rule is to report the first applicable code in order; E3 precedes E5 in the list, so E3 would be the first code that applies since there is no control group without generative AI). Given the code order, E3 is the first applicable code.

title: Leveraging Large Language Model for Automatic Translation of Educational Content: Exploring the Effectiveness of Curriculum-Aware Prompt Engineering
rationale: Abstract concerns LLM-based translation of assessment items compared across two prompt strategies, with expert reviews and linguistic feature comparison. This is not a learner-facing STEM learning activity, no learning outcome or learner control group is described, and the content is educational translation rather than STEM. Excluded on the first applicable code E2 (content not STEM), since the study is about translation of assessment items rather than STEM learning; the abstract gives positive evidence that the content domain is not STEM. Note that E1 could also arguably apply because the LLM is used by researchers/translators rather than learners.

title: Evaluation of the performance and temporal variability of large language models in patient education regarding pneumothorax: a seven-day analysis
rationale: The study evaluates LLM chatbot outputs about pneumothorax patient education, rated by thoracic surgeons. The content is medical/patient education, not STEM under the protocol's domain list (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), and health professions/patient health information falls outside the domain. There is no learner interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity, and no control group without generative AI is evident; the design is a set of repeated chatbot output evaluations. E2 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly met on abstract evidence; the abstract gives positive evidence the content is medical rather than STEM education.

title: Evaluating the Accuracy and Reliability of Large Language Models (ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, Grok, and Le Chat) in Answering Item-Analyzed Multiple-Choice Questions on Blood Physiology
rationale: The LLMs themselves were tested on the MCQ items; learners did not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity. Students took the MCQ test but no LLM group was compared with a non-AI control. The design is a cross-sectional evaluation of LLM accuracy, not a controlled comparison. E1 applies as the first failing code: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

title: INVESTIGATING THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON CREATIVE WRITING SKILLS AMONG UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN SIALKOT
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive, questionnaire-only study of students' perceptions (PU/PEOU) of AI tools. No control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions only. Domain is English creative writing, which is non-STEM, so E2 could also apply, but E5 is the earliest code supported by the abstract's positive evidence (perception-only outcome). Coding E5 as the first applicable code in protocol order: E1 is not clearly failed at abstract stage, E2 is arguably met as non-STEM content, so the first clearly applicable code should be E2. Final code applied: E2 is the earliest positive failure of a criterion in order after E1 cannot be determined; see rationale.

title: ChatGPT as a Writing Aid: Opportunities and Challenges in Developing Students’ Logical Reasoning Skills
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative design with surveys and interviews of 15 students, with no control or comparison group. Perception-based findings (93.3% perceive benefit) are not a quantitative learning outcome. Design and comparison fail on positive evidence, so E3 is the first applicable code. Domain is also unclear (English education writing, not STEM), but E3 is reported as the first code that applies under the ordering.

title: A DESCRIPTIVE ANALYSIS OF UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS’ CONTINUANCE INTENTION TOWARD CHATGPT USE IN MALAYSIAN HIGHER EDUCATION
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive cross-sectional survey of perceptions (UTAUT2 constructs) with no control group, no randomization, and no quantitative learning outcome. It states that no causal relationships are inferred. Positive evidence of failing design, comparison, and outcome criteria is present, so it is excluded. E6 is used as the first applicable code under the protocol's order, since the study is a survey (non-experimental) rather than an empirical learning study; the protocol lists survey designs under design exclusions, and the closest code is E6 (not an empirical study eligible for the review). Outcome is perceptions only, which would also fail E5, but E6 comes first in the sequence given the descriptive survey design.

title: Exploring the Utilisation of Generative AI Tools by Undergraduate First-Year Mechanical Engineering Students in Programming Assessments.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive investigation of students' Gen AI tool use in a programming assessment, with no separate control group without generative AI and no reported comparative learning outcome. Positive evidence of no control group supports E3 at abstract stage. Population (first-year undergraduates), domain (Python programming) and intervention (student use of Gen AI tools) appear eligible. Exclusion is based on the abstract's descriptive usage-survey framing; the full text should be checked if there is any doubt about a comparison arm.

title: Prompt engineering for improving foreign language skills of technical university students
rationale: The study concerns foreign language learning, which the protocol explicitly excludes as non-STEM content (E2). Generative AI use via prompt engineering is indicated, but the domain failure is clear from the abstract, so the record is excluded on E2 without needing to assess the other criteria.

title: An LLM-Driven Chatbot in Higher Education for Databases and Information Systems
rationale: At abstract stage there is positive evidence of no control group: the study reports a single-group deployment of MoodleBot with TAM questionnaire and accuracy measures, with no comparison condition described. Outcomes are perceptions (TAM acceptance) and response accuracy rather than a quantitative learning outcome, which also points away from eligibility. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 is a secondary concern. Note the abstract stage rule is to exclude only on positive evidence; the absence of any comparison group described is the basis here.

title: Toward hybrid teaching intelligence: investigating the potential of teacher–AI collaboration using large language models
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of in-service Norwegian teachers about LLM use. It is not an empirical experimental study with a control group or learner learning outcome, and participants are teachers rather than students. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) applies, as the design is qualitative and does not measure learning outcomes. Coded as E6 since the qualitative design is non-eligible per the design criterion; population (in-service teachers) would also fail.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) in dental education: Opportunities, cautions, and recommendations
rationale: The record is a perspective article that explicitly states no evidence exists on GenAI effects on critical thinking in dental students. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also has no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Dental education is health-professions content, which would also fail the domain criterion, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given (E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education: Balancing Opportunities, Risks, and Ethical Challenges in the Era of Generative AI
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails the eligibility criteria on design and outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also a review, which could alternatively be E10, but the review design is the more direct failure.

title: Navigating The Dependency Of College Students Using AI Chatbots For Language Learning: A Phenomenology
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenology with five interviewees and no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is language learning, which is non-STEM. The sequence is E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6, so the first applicable code is E2 and that is the code reported. Reporting E2 as the first applicable code in the protocol's order.

title: Generative AI in Technology-Oriented Higher Education: A Systematized Review and Survey on Students’ Perceptions of Performance, Autonomy, and Ethical Implications
rationale: The record is a systematized literature review plus a cross-sectional anonymous survey of students. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and reports perceptions and usage rather than a quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study meeting the design criteria. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly established from the abstract, and E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable code given the review-and-survey design. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the design and outcome criteria fail.

title: Exploring the impact of GenAI-assisted EFL courses on foreign language anxiety and willingness to communicate: a disciplinary comparison
rationale: Study is about GenAI-assisted EFL (English as a foreign language) courses, with outcomes foreign language anxiety and willingness to communicate. Content is language learning, which the protocol explicitly excludes from the STEM domain. Accounting and electrical engineering students are the disciplinary comparison groups, but the taught content is English language, not STEM content. Exclusion code E2 applies. Affective outcomes (FLA, WTC) would also not be extracted under the protocol.

title: Assessing the effectiveness of large language models for generating and estimating time complexity of code segments
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Llama) on generating and analyzing C code segments of given time complexity, with the LLM itself being the object of evaluation. There is no learner-facing intervention and no control group of learners without generative AI; the comparison is between LLMs and performance is measured on model output correctness, not on student learning. Exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order given the design, though E1 (not learner-facing) could also apply; the abstract shows only model-vs-model evaluation with no comparison group.

title: Exploring Students’ Preferences and Satisfaction in Using Digital Media for Arabic Language Learning in Islamic Higher Education
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of student preferences and satisfaction with digital media. It has no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome (only preferences and satisfaction). Arabic language learning is also non-STEM. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention is clearly not learner-facing generative AI, which is unclear here, so E2 would be first if content is non-STEM. Note: Under the stated order, the first applicable code is E2 because Arabic language learning is non-STEM, so E2 is the correct code. Design and outcome failures also apply but are later in order.

title: USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR ACADEMIC PURPOSES AMONG UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS: A PILOT STUDY
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of perceptions and tool use among Ayurveda (BAMS) students. It has no control group, no experimental manipulation, and no quantitative learning outcome; it measures perceptions and usage only. Domain is also health/medical (Ayurveda), not STEM. Excluded at the first applicable code, E6 (not an empirical intervention study in the protocol sense); note that E6 is applied as the design is cross-sectional survey rather than an eligible comparative design.

title: Generative AI as a Catalyst for Financial Learning in Vocational Training
rationale: The abstract describes a single group measured before and after using generative AI (baseline test, then repeated test). No separate control group without generative AI is described, so E3 applies. Financial literacy is also arguably not STEM (E2 would be a secondary concern), but E3 is the first applicable code in order. Positive evidence of a within-subject pre-post design is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

title: Research on Teaching of Structural Safety Judgment for Railway Vehicles Driven by Controlled Errors of Generative Artificial Intelligence
rationale: Abstract describes a teaching framework and illustrative worked examples; it explicitly states that no classroom teaching effectiveness is measured, and the learning benefits 'still need to be validated by real classroom data'. The model-based estimates (87.5% underestimation, dynamic load factor) are not learner outcomes. Exclusion is on E5 at the abstract stage because there is positive evidence that no learning outcome was measured. Design and comparison also appear not met, but the first applicable code in order is E5 (E3 would precede E5 if the control-group absence were treated as primary; the abstract gives no control group, so E5 is recorded per the explicit statement). Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by the explicit absence of classroom data.

title: The Effect of Generative AI Dependency on Academic Integrity among Postgraduate Students at KPPIM
rationale: Survey-based correlational design (regression on DAI and AIS scales) with no control group comparing generative AI use against non-AI use. Outcome is self-reported dependency and academic integrity perceptions, not a quantitative learning measure. Domain is not clearly STEM. Exclude under E3 as the first applicable code in order: no comparison group without generative AI. Note that the design and outcome also fail, but the E3 code is the first that applies in the specified order.
