title: Students' Perceptions about the Impact of AI Chatbots on their Vocabulary and Grammar in EFL Writing
rationale: The study concerns EFL writing (English language learning), which is non-STEM content, so it fails the Domain criterion (E2). The abstract also describes a perception-based mixed-methods survey with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3 and E5 as well; E2 is reported first per the code order.

title: Assessing students’ DRIVE: A framework to evaluate learning through interactions with generative AI
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational analysis of GenAI interaction annotations against essay scores in STEM writing courses, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Its design is correlational, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion is coded E3 (no control group without generative AI), the first applicable code in the protocol's order beyond E1/E2 (E2 is unclear from the abstract alone and was not used).

title: Generative AI vs. future competencies of Nigerian public university students
rationale: The study is a qualitative design (focus groups and interviews with 12 students) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study that meets the comparison or design criteria. Exclusion code E6 is used as the first applicable code given the qualitative, non-experimental design. Note: E3 and E5 would also apply; E6 is reported as the most fundamental reason since it is a qualitative study, but the order in the protocol places E1 first, and the intervention (GenAI use) is not clearly described as learner-facing within a learning activity.

title: Designing Practical Entrepreneurship: A Case Study of an Online Entrepreneurship Course for Secondary Students
rationale: The record is a design case study describing development and pilot of an entrepreneurship course, drawing on surveys, interviews and reflections. It reports no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study. Entrepreneurship is also not clearly STEM content. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code at the abstract stage on the basis of the design-case framing; E5 and E3 would also apply. Generative AI is mentioned only as tools students negotiated, so intervention status is unclear.

title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in Enhancing Self-Learning and Developing Employees’ Digital Skills: An Applied Study in the Oil Products Distribution Authority in the Middle Euphrates Region
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive analytical study using a questionnaire and interviews with employees of an oil products distribution authority. Population is workplace employees, not K-12 or higher education students (E4). The design is a survey/descriptive study with no control group, and there is no experimental learning outcome. Exclusion is based on the population criterion; the abstract gives positive evidence that the sample is employees in a workplace setting.

title: Disciplinary And Gender Differences In Students’ Perceptions of ChatGPT For Academic Assignments: A Case of Universitas Negeri Semarang
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods perception survey with interviews and no control group, and it reports only perceptions and attitudes rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Design and comparison criteria are not met on the abstract's description. Under the protocol, E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) applies as the first failing code in order (E1 and E2 are not clearly failed; E3 would also apply, but E5 is the clearest positive evidence of a non-learning-outcome design). The domain is also not clearly STEM. Excluding on E5 given the abstract's explicit description of perceptions only.

title: A Case Study of Teaching-Learning Strategies Using Generative Artificial Intelligence in a Problem-Based Learning Program for Fashion Marketing
rationale: Abstract describes a single-group design-based case study with pre-post surveys (17 of 35 students completing both), with no control group. Content is fashion marketing, which is not STEM. Exclusion is on E2 (not STEM), the first applicable code in protocol order; the abstract also gives no evidence of a comparison group (E3), and the design is a case study rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental design. No quote is strictly needed beyond the domain; the abstract's "six-week educational program" and "fashion marketing education" describe the content.

title: Exploring medical students’ intention to use of ChatGPT from a programming course: a grounded theory study in China
rationale: The study is a grounded theory qualitative design based on interviews of 30 students. It has no control group without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion uses the first applicable code in order; E1 does not apply because ChatGPT is learner-facing, and E2 does not apply because programming is STEM. E3 is the first failing criterion in the list, since the design has no comparison group. E6 (not an empirical study) would also fit as a qualitative design, but the abstract shows empirical interview data, so E3 is the most direct code.

title: DATA-DRIVEN EDUCATION IN UNIVERSITY PHYSICS: A COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS OF LEARNING ANALYTICS DASHBOARDS AND AI TUTORING
rationale: The abstract describes a review/synthesis article (international case studies, theory, synthesized survey data) rather than an empirical experiment with a control group. No randomized or quasi-experimental comparison is evident, so the study is not an empirical study meeting the design criterion. Exclusion code E6 applies as the first failing code given the protocol's ordering (E1 and E2 are not clearly failed at abstract stage; E6 is the most direct positive evidence of failure).

title: Students’ Use and Perception of Educational GenAI Chatbot in High School Computing: Insights from the Decomposed Theory of Planned Behavior
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of perceptions and intentions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is reported as the first applicable code in order. Although E5 and E6 would also apply, E3 (no control group) is the first in the protocol's listed order that fits the design, so the record is excluded. Clearly no eligibility criterion is met by the design or outcome.

title: CHATGPT IN ACADEMIA: AN IN-DEPTH EXPLORATION OF STUDENT VIEWS – PROS AND CONS
rationale: The abstract describes an overview/discussion paper on student views of ChatGPT ("pros and cons"). It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it does not appear to be an empirical study. Excluded under E6 on positive evidence from the abstract. The STEM domain is also not specified. Exclusion is based on the absence of any empirical design in the abstract.

title: Effectiveness of AI in solving math problems at the secondary school level
rationale: Abstract compares ChatGPT's accuracy against ten students' accuracy on the same 20 math questions. This is a performance comparison of AI versus humans, not a learner-facing intervention with a separate control group that does not use generative AI. No randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group is described. Positive evidence of no eligible control group, so exclude under E3 at abstract stage. Note that the code applied is E3 per the protocol's first-failing-criterion order; the intervention criterion is also doubtful (students do not interact with AI as a learning activity as described).

title: The association between generative artificial intelligence use and foreign language classroom anxiety
rationale: Abstract stage, but there is positive evidence of a failed criterion. The domain is foreign language learning (English proficiency, foreign language classroom anxiety), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies first. The design is a correlational/regression survey with no control group and no learning outcome, so it would also fail E3, E5 and E6. Only the first applicable code is reported.

title: Exploring nursing students' motivation for generative AI use: Academic libraries and AI literacy instruction
rationale: The title indicates a study of nursing students' motivation for generative AI use, which is a motivation/perception focus and not an evaluated STEM learning intervention. Nursing is health professions education, which the protocol excludes from the domain criterion. No abstract is available. The exclusion is based on the title only: nursing is health professions education (domain not met), and there is no evidence of a STEM learning outcome or a control group. Because the abstract stage excludes only on positive evidence, this exclusion rests on the title's clear health-professions domain. Coded E4 as the population/domain mismatch; E2 could also apply, and the audit may prefer E2 because the domain criterion is the one actually failing.

title: Implementation of Project-Based Learning Using Generative AI for Designing Environmental Research Posters
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pre-test/post-test design with no separate control group without generative AI, which is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (E3). Exclusion is made at abstract stage on this basis, as the design is explicitly single-group.

title: AS-1011-26 Resolution on Course Syllabi
rationale: The record is an Academic Senate policy resolution about the content of course syllabi, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no comparison group, no design, and no learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies first in the code order that reaches a fundamental failure; E1 would also arguably apply since no learner interacts with generative AI, but the record is a policy document, so E6 is the most accurate primary code.

title: Redefining creativity differences for art students who use and those who do not use GenAI: evidence from network analysis
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional network analysis comparing students who use GenAI with those who do not, based on students enrolled in art programs. Art creativity is not STEM content, so E2 applies first. There is no indication of a randomized or quasi-experimental design with an intervention and control group, and no quantitative learning outcome is evident (creativity features from network analysis). Exclusion is clear on domain at the abstract stage.

title: Medical Student Perspectives on the Recommended Considerations for Interacting With ChatGPT as Part of Learning and Working With Patients
rationale: The record is a reflective opinion piece proposing a Code of Practice, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also medical education, which falls under the health professions exclusion. E6 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported, so it is used here.

title: Beyond initial adoption of generative AI: the role of AI performance and comfort expectancy in driving ChatGPT continuance among students at Indonesian universities
rationale: Survey-based cross-sectional study using PLS-SEM on continuance intention. No randomized or quasi-experimental design with a non-generative-AI control group, and no quantitative learning outcome (continuance intention is a perception/usage measure). Excluded at first applicable code E3 (no control group without generative AI). The protocol's design and outcome criteria also fail, but E3 is the first code in order that applies. Domain is not stated in the abstract, so it is not assessed as a basis for exclusion.

title: UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS' PERCEPTION ON USING CHATGPT FOR IDEA DEVELOPMENT IN ACADEMIC WRITING BASED ON TAM: A DESCRIPTIVE STUDY
rationale: placeholder

title: It Helps with Crap Lecturers and Their Low Effort: Investigating Computer Science Students’ Perceptions of Using ChatGPT for Learning
rationale: This is a mixed-methods survey study of computing students' perceptions and trust in ChatGPT. It reports no learning outcome, only perceptions and usage, and has no control group. Design is a survey, not an experiment. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome); the abstract gives positive evidence of perception-only measures. Although E3 and E6 might also apply, E5 is the first code in the protocol order that clearly fails on the abstract.

title: Supporting Students With Disabilities to Use Generative AI: A Classroom-Based Taxonomy of Educator Scaffolding Practices
rationale: The abstract describes a collaborative action research study with video-based analysis producing a qualitative taxonomy. There is no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E1 check: the intervention is learner-facing ChatGPT use, so E1 does not apply. E2 does not apply (science classroom). E3 applies because there is no control group without generative AI. Under the protocol order, E3 is the first applicable code after E1 and E2, so the exclusion code should be E3 rather than E6. The qualitative design is also evident, but the report must use the first applicable code in order.

title: Perceptions and Self-Regulation on the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Science Learning of Science, Technology and Engineering (STE) Students of Dasmariñas Integrated High School
rationale: Descriptive-quantitative study of student perceptions and self-regulation with descriptive statistics, ANOVA and Pearson correlation; no control group without generative AI is described, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Outcomes are perceptions and usage rather than a quantitative learning measure (E5 also plausible). Per the order of codes, E1 is not clearly established from the abstract, and E3 is the first clearly applicable code since no comparison group exists. Population (senior high STE students) and domain (science) appear met.

title: Management course design quality, feedback literacy, and judgment-oriented learning in AI-rich business school classrooms: Evidence from Taiwan
rationale: Record has no abstract. Title indicates a business school management course context (management education, feedback literacy, judgment-oriented learning), which is not STEM content under the protocol. Exclusion on domain is supported by the title alone; no quote is available from an abstract. Note that the protocol's E1 code is checked first, but the record gives no evidence about whether the AI is learner-facing or generative, so E2 is the first code with positive evidence of failure. Flagging for researcher review given the thin record.

title: Envisioning the future of learning and teaching engineering in the artificial intelligence era: Opportunities and challenges
rationale: The record reads as a position/perspective piece ("Envisioning the future of learning and teaching engineering... Opportunities and challenges"). The abstract describes potential benefits of generative AI and does not report any empirical study, sample, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. There is positive evidence it is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Note that E6 is ordered before E3/E5, and the abstract gives no positive evidence of an experiment.

title: Exploring the Adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence by TVET Students: A UTAUT Analysis of Perceptions, Benefits, and Implementation Challenges
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of 200 TVET students using UTAUT constructs (perceptions, intentions) with regression. No experimental control group, and the only outcome is perceived/behavioral intention rather than a quantitative learning measure. Survey design and perception-only outcomes fail the protocol. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome); the design also fails, but the first applicable code in order is E5 given the outcome is perception-only. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of failure, exclusion is appropriate even at the abstract stage.

title: How students make sense of ChatGPT in digital literacy education: reflections on ethics, dependency, emotion, and evaluation
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative content analysis of student self-reflection texts, with no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a non-empirical-quantitative qualitative design, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the closest code for a qualitative study that does not meet the protocol's design requirements; the abstract gives positive evidence that the design is qualitative and not a comparison study. Domain (digital literacy, not clearly STEM) is also unclear.

title: Исследование эффективности промпт-инжиниринга и квантованных LLM в создании структуры академических курсов
rationale: The abstract describes LLMs used to generate university course structures, with outputs compared against ChatGPT-4. Learners do not appear to interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity; the LLMs seem to be used for curriculum development (a teacher/designer-side task). There is also no evident learner-level quantitative learning outcome, and no control group without generative AI is described (the comparison is between LLM variants). Positive evidence of failure on intervention (learner-facing use) is present, so exclude at E1 per the first applicable code. Record is in Russian with an English abstract; language was not used for exclusion at abstract stage.

title: Mass Generation of Programming Learning Problems from Public Code Repositories
rationale: The abstract describes an automatic generator of programming problems validated by automatically solving them in an ITS and expert ratings. No learner interacts with a generative AI tool, there is no control group, and no learning outcome is reported. The generator is template/randomization-based with LLMs mentioned only as a comparison method in the related approaches. Excluded on E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code in the order; the intervention itself is also not learner-facing generative AI (E1 would arguably apply first). Per the code order, E1 is the first applicable code, so this should be considered. Note: applying the strict order, the correct code is E1.

title: The use of artificial intelligence in the individualization of student learning in higher technical educational institutions
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical analysis, comparative analysis of platforms, and generalization of institutional experience. It reports no controlled comparison, no design meeting the protocol's experimental/quasi-experimental requirement, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence that the record is not an empirical comparative study supports E6. Domain is not specified as STEM in the abstract, but E6 applies first in the code order as written (E1 and E2 are not positively shown to fail at abstract level).

title: Leveraging Generative Artificial Intelligence to Enhance Mathematical Innovation and Practical Abilities of University Students
rationale: The abstract describes an analysis of the current application status, advantages, challenges, and strategies of GenAI in mathematics education, with no empirical study, sample, comparison group, or quantitative outcome reported. It reads as a discussion/review paper, so it is not an empirical study (E6). The abstract gives positive evidence of no empirical design, which supports exclusion at this stage.

title: Telehealth Simulations with Generative Artificial Intelligence in Midwifery Education: Practice for Person‐Centered and Culturally Responsive Care
rationale: Midwifery education with a generative AI avatar simulation for telehealth and cultural responsiveness. Content is midwifery/clinical care, not a STEM domain under the protocol (health professions education is excluded). Abstract describes a pilot with student learning assessed but no control group or quantitative comparison is reported, so comparison and design are not met on the abstract. Exclusion code E2 is applied as the first failing criterion for the health-professions domain. The abstract does not state the design explicitly, but the domain exclusion alone is sufficient.

title: Analysis and Research on the Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Engineering Programming Courses
rationale: The abstract describes a position/reform-proposal paper ("this paper proposes comprehensive reform suggestions"). It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under rule 2, exclusion requires positive evidence of failure; here the abstract itself indicates a non-empirical discussion paper, so E6 applies. Note that E6 is the first applicable code in order only if E1 is not clearly failing; the abstract does not clearly show a learner-facing tool, so E1 was not assigned.

title: To Develop Clothing Life Lesson Plans by Prospective Elementary School Teacher Using the ChatGPT
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group qualitative study of 19 pre-service teachers using ChatGPT, with findings based on feedback and comparative analysis of lesson plans and reports. There is no control group without generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Excluded under E3 (no comparison group); the design is also not an experiment. Domain (clothing life/practical arts) is also not clearly STEM. The first applicable code in order is E3, since E1 does not apply (learners do use ChatGPT).

title: Guiding the uncharted: the emerging (and missing) policies on Generative AI in higher education
rationale: The study is a document analysis of institutional policies and guidelines (policy review and content analysis of curricula), not an empirical experiment or quasi-experiment. It has no learner-facing GenAI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study) on the abstract's own description. Earlier codes such as E1 or E3 would also fit, but E6 is the most direct reason; the code order rule places E1 first, and the abstract gives positive evidence that the study does not evaluate a learner-facing tool, so E1 could also apply. Reporting E6 as the core design failure.

title: Evaluating Generative AI for Depression Diagnosis: Implications for Counselor Education and Supervision
rationale: The study evaluates generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) diagnosing depression from clinical case descriptions. The content is mental health/clinical diagnosis, which falls under health professions education and is not STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. There is also no evident control group without generative AI, and the AI is not shown to be learner-facing, but E2 is the first applicable code. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

title: Indonesian EFL Learners Responses to Using ChatGPT: An Analysis Based on The TAM Model
rationale: This is a cross-sectional survey (TAM questionnaire, CFA, perceptions of ChatGPT) with no control group and no learning outcome; it measures perceptions and attitudes only. Domain is English language learning, which is non-STEM. Exclusion code E5 applies as the first failing criterion for this abstract-stage record, since the outcome is perceptions/attitudes rather than a quantitative learning measure. The E2 (non-STEM) and E3 (no control) failures also apply, but the protocol asks for the first code in order; E2 precedes E5 in the list, so E2 is the more accurate first code. Correcting to E2 below.

title: Generative AI as a catalyst for next-generation medical education: innovation, ethics, and implementation
rationale: The title frames the paper around medical education, which is a health professions context and falls under the protocol's domain exclusion (health professions education is not STEM). The record has no abstract, so this rests on the title alone. The title also suggests a conceptual or perspective piece ("innovation, ethics, and implementation") rather than an empirical study, but that is not clear from the title. Excluding at abstract stage on E2 is justified by the title's explicit medical focus; the rule to exclude only on positive evidence is met because the title itself names medical education.

title: How does collaborative prompting behaviour develop and relate to effectiveness in problem-solving with Generative Artificial Intelligence?
rationale: Abstract describes a correlational study of group prompting behaviour and task effectiveness across groups with unrestricted GenAI access. There is no control group without generative AI, and no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison is described. Association-based analysis indicates the design fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 applies (no control group without generative AI). Domain (mystery-solving task) is not clearly STEM. Abstract-stage evidence of the missing comparison is sufficient to exclude.

title: APPLICATION OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE METHODICAL WORK OF A UNIVERSITY TEACHER: DEVELOPMENT OF TEST MATERIALS
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT-4o used by a university teacher to generate test materials (tasks, test questions, synopses). This is teacher-facing use of generative AI to prepare materials, not learner-facing use, so E1 applies. There is no indication of a learner-interaction intervention or a control group with learning outcomes. Excluding at the abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

title: ChatGPT: the future of discharge summaries?
rationale: The record is a Lancet Digital Health commentary/viewpoint on using ChatGPT to write hospital discharge summaries. It reports no empirical study, no control group, no learners, and no outcome data. It is not an empirical study (E6). It is also not about STEM learning and involves clinicians rather than students, but E6 is the first applicable code in order from E1 onward only if E1 and earlier do not apply. The intervention is clinician-facing rather than learner-facing, which would technically be E1 first; however, the record is not an empirical study at all, so E6 is the most fundamental reason. Decision is exclude at abstract stage with positive evidence of no empirical design.

title: Revitalizing STEM Education: integrating STEM into National curricula with active learning
rationale: At abstract stage, the intervention is low-code programming scenarios for mobile apps; no learner-facing generative AI tool is described. The abstract mentions generative AI only as background motivation. Positive evidence that the intervention is not generative AI supports exclusion under E1. Results rely on educator perceptions and surveys, with no clear quantitative learning outcome (E5 also a possible concern). Control classes are mentioned but the abstract does not describe a comparison of learning outcomes.

title: Knowledge, Attitude, and Practices Towards Chatgpt of Senior High School Mathematics Learners
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-style study of knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward ChatGPT among senior high school mathematics learners. It reports group differences in perceptions and self-reported use, not a learning outcome, and there is no experimental or comparison group with a learning intervention. Design is a survey and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Coding the first applicable exclusion in order: E1 is not clearly applicable since the abstract does not state whether the tool is learner-facing in a learning activity, but the decisive failure is the absence of a control group and a learning outcome. Per the protocol order, the first code that applies from E1 onward would be E1 only if intervention failure is evident; the abstract gives no positive evidence that the intervention is non-generative, so the strongest positive evidence is the lack of a control group (E3) and of a learning outcome (E5). Using E3 as the first clearly evidenced failure. Note that the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group, so exclusion is supported.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Utilization and Productivity Among English Teachers in Selected Private Higher Education Institutions in Laguna
rationale: The participants are in-service English teachers, not K-12 or higher education students, so E4 applies. The design is a correlational survey with no control group and the outcome is teacher productivity perceptions rather than a learner quantitative outcome. Domain is English language teaching, which is non-STEM. Exclusion code reports the first applicable code in order; E1 (learner-facing intervention) is also doubtful, but E4 is clearly positive from the abstract. Note the quote was condensed with ellipses from the abstract text.

title: Implementing ChatGPT as Tutor, Tutee, and Tool in Physics and Chemistry
rationale: The abstract describes a narrative review of ChatGPT implementations in physics and chemistry education. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is therefore not an empirical study (E6). The review also has no reported comparison or design, so E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

title: A PROPOSED VISION FOR DEVELOPING KINDERGARTEN PROGRAMS IN THE KINGDOM OF SAUDI ARABIA IN LIGHT OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE APPLICATIONS
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of teachers, supervisors and specialists about generative AI use in kindergartens. It has no experimental or comparison group, no learner-facing intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an empirical intervention study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the primary failing; the design is a questionnaire survey, which the protocol also excludes. Population is teachers/specialists, not students, and the domain is not STEM.

title: What are we telling our students about AI? An exploratory analysis of university instructors’ generative AI syllabi policies
rationale: The study is a content analysis of 92 syllabus policy documents, not an empirical experiment with learners interacting with a generative AI tool. There is no comparison group and no learning outcome measure. Exclude as not an empirical study under E6 (the record's own design is a document content analysis, which is outside the protocol's eligible designs). Note that E1 (intervention not learner-facing) would also apply, but E6 is the first code in order that fits the design. The first-applicable-code rule is E1 first; however, the abstract gives positive evidence that the work is a document analysis rather than an empirical learner study, so E6 is reported as the primary basis.

title: The copy and paste culture in the age of Generative AI: Implications for academic writing skills among English students in South-south Nigeria
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of English students' self-reported copy-and-paste practices and correlations with writing competencies. There is no learner-facing generative AI intervention assigned to groups, no control group, and no experimental design. The study is not an empirical trial meeting the protocol's design criteria, and the domain (English/academic writing) is non-STEM. Exclusion at E6 reflects that it is a survey (non-empirical-experimental) design; the first applicable code in order would arguably be E1 or E2 since the intervention and domain fail, but the abstract-stage rule requires positive evidence and the strongest is the non-STEM domain. Coding per protocol order: E1 is the first code that applies on the intervention (no AI tool used as part of a learning activity under study; usage was self-reported survey). Given the ordering, the correct first applicable code is E1.

title: Perspective of Science Educators and Students on the Use of ChatGPT: A Study of Artificial Intelligence
rationale: The study is a survey of perceptions of ChatGPT use, with descriptive and comparative statistics. It has no control group and no learning outcome measure; it reports perceptions only. Design is survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not strictly the right fit, but the closest first-applicable code given the protocol's ordering would be E3 for no comparison group. Per the protocol order, E1 does not clearly apply (ChatGPT use is learner-facing in classroom), E2 unclear. The first clearly failing criterion is the absence of a control group (E3). Reporting E3 as the primary code is the more accurate ordering-based choice.

title: Unpacking GenAI-enabled deep learning engagement: role perceptions, human–GenAI synergy strategies, and underlying mechanisms
rationale: Abstract describes a mixed-methods correlational design (path analysis and latent profile analysis of reflection reports from 181 undergraduates) with no described control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition. Positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails: no comparison group is described, and the design is correlational/qualitative rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Excluded under E3 at abstract stage.

title: AI as a Procedural Equalizer: Performance Comparison in Programming-Based Engineering Coursework Following the Emergence of Generative AI
rationale: The abstract describes a retrospective pre/post comparison across time periods (pre-AI vs post-AI cohorts) rather than a separate concurrent control group without generative AI. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group and a single-group historical design fails the comparison and design criteria, so E3 applies. Students' actual use of generative AI is also not clearly described as a learner-facing intervention. Domain (programming) and outcome (project scores) appear to be met.

title: The Role of Generative AI (ChatGPT) in Computer Science Education
rationale: The abstract reads as a narrative or conceptual discussion of ChatGPT in computer science education ("This paper explores the role...", "The paper concludes..."). It gives no description of an empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative outcome. Positive evidence of a non-empirical paper is present, so it is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Design, comparison, and outcome are not reported in the abstract.

title: STEM Education and AI Applications in Chemistry Teaching: From Pedagogical Ecosystems to the Self-Efficacy of Secondary School Teachers
rationale: Abstract describes a conceptual framework plus an "exemplary case study" of a chemistry STEM project with three layers, including LLM (ChatGPT) use. No control group, comparison design, or quantitative learning outcome is reported; the study appears to be a conceptual/case description rather than an empirical experiment. Positive evidence that the design fails (no comparison group, case study) supports exclusion. Coded E6 as not an empirical study, though the design-based exclusion (no control group) is also a plausible reading; the abstract gives no comparison group.

title: The Design and Implementation of an Educational Chatbot with Personalized Adaptive Learning Features for Project Management Training
rationale: The study builds a generative-AI chatbot (PMTutor) for project management training. Project management is not a STEM domain under the protocol (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), so E2 applies. The abstract also emphasises usability and feedback rather than a controlled comparison with a learning outcome, but the domain failure alone is sufficient for exclusion.

title: Demystifying Generative Artificial Intelligence in Academic Classrooms: Students’ Attitude and Critical Thinking
rationale: The abstract describes a convergent mixed-methods study using a descriptive survey and semi-structured interviews on student attitudes and perceived impact on critical thinking. It reports no separate control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning measure; outcomes are perceptions. Exclusion at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code in order that is supported by positive evidence; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3), but E5 is listed earlier in the code order only after E1-E4 are checked, and E3 would apply first. Note: per protocol order, the first applicable code is E3 because no control group is described. Since the protocol requires the first applicable code in order, the code is E3.

title: Postgraduate EFL Writing with GenAI across Scientific Domains: A Qualitative Approach to Faculty and Doctoral Student Feedback
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative study of participant feedback (in-class discussions, annotated tasks, final survey) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is EFL academic writing, not STEM content, and the abstract does not show a comparison. Outcomes are perceptions and attitudes (learning attitude, ratings of understanding), not a quantitative learning measure. Domain is not STEM-specific as stated. Exclusion code E3 applied as the first failing criterion for the comparison/design requirement; the design is a survey, which also fails E6 territory, but the protocol's first-applicable ordering places no-control-group (E3) first among the design-related failures. Abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design, so exclusion is warranted.

rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of six students' perceptions. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and translation is a language-learning domain rather than STEM. The design is not an empirical experiment meeting the protocol; E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs) is the best fit, though E2 (non-STEM content) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) also apply. Per the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E1 does not apply clearly, E2 would be the first code that clearly applies on domain. Correcting: the first applicable code in order is E2, since translation/language learning is not STEM.

No control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported; the chi-square and Fisher tests relate metaphor roles to cognitive influence categories, not learning measures. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the most direct code given that outcomes are perceptual. Design also lacks a control group (E3 could apply), but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given the perception-only outcome. Abstract stage evidence is positive for failure of outcome criterion.

Also, the study measures perceptions and acceptance rather than a learning outcome and reports no control group (E3/E5 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E2 only if domain is checked before others; E1 is not clearly failed at abstract stage. Domain failure is the clearest positive evidence.

title: Undergraduate Students’ Perspectives towards Using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its Integration into their Learning in the English as a Foreign Language Program
rationale: The study is a single online survey of students' perspectives with no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an empirical experimental study meeting the protocol. EFL content is also not STEM. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the design criteria) as the first applicable code in the order set by the protocol's structure, since the design is a survey, not a comparative study. Note the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design, so exclusion is justified.

rationale: Abstract describes an engineering STEM approach to obtaining and processing sound data with Raspberry Pi, and discusses generative AI only as motivation. It gives no evidence of a learner-facing generative AI intervention, a control group, or any quantitative learning outcome. Design is not described as an experiment. Positive evidence of failing criteria exists for the outcome (none reported) and design (no comparison described), so exclusion is warranted at the abstract stage. Coded E5 as the outcome criterion is the clearest failure; the record may also fail E1 and E3 at fulltext.

title: The Use of Generative AI in Clinical Learning Activities and Its Relationship on Student Nurses’ Caring Practices
rationale: The study is a descriptive-correlational survey with a single sample of students who all had prior generative AI exposure; there is no control group without generative AI, and no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. Correlation between self-reported AI use frequency and caring practices is not an eligible design. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies as the first failing criterion in order that is clearly evidenced; the design also fails the protocol's Design criterion, but E3 is the code assigned by the protocol order for missing comparison.

title: Optimizing educational analytics by analyzing student perceptions of ChatGPT in programming education using enhanced feature selection
rationale: The study analyzes student perception questionnaire data with a feature selection algorithm and classifiers (SVM, k-NN). There is no learning outcome measure and no control group comparing generative AI use with a non-AI condition. Perceptions-only outcomes fail the outcome criterion, so exclude at E5. Exclusion code E5 applies because the only measure is perception, which the protocol excludes.

The abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content (Spanish language education and AI literacy framed as foreign language education), so E2 applies as the first failing code. No quote is used as the supporting passage is the setting description; quote is null.

Also the design is a survey with correlational regression and interviews, not an experiment with a control group. Exclusion code E2 is the first applicable code in order to report, since the domain fails regardless of design. Decision made at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

title: Language Learning Motivation of Form Six Students Preparing for MUET in Kota Kinabalu
rationale: The study concerns English language learning motivation via a descriptive questionnaire survey. No generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome are described. Content is English language learning, which is non-STEM. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not generative AI) which also applies; however, the primary and most direct failure is non-STEM content. Per code order, the first applicable code is E1 since no learner-facing generative AI is present.

rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study in which open-ended questions were posed to ChatGPT. There is no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is qualitative, so it fails the design criterion. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not the best fit. The study is an empirical qualitative study, so the closest code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Given the protocol's ordering, E3 is the most accurate first-applicable code. The record is therefore excluded under E3.

rationale: The study is a qualitative interview and survey design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study eligible under the protocol. Health professions education is also excluded by the domain criterion. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, with a qualitative design outside the eligible designs) is applied as the first applicable code given the design. Abstract stage is sufficient for exclusion because the design is positively stated as qualitative.

rationale: The content is English as a foreign language (language learning, non-STEM), which fails the domain criterion. Additionally, the outcome is coverage of feedback categories as present/absent rather than a learning measure, and there is no evident learning-outcome comparison; these are secondary concerns. rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory study in which ChatGPT and Gemini were used to answer assessment items. There is no learner-facing use of generative AI and no comparison group, so this is not an empirical comparison of learning outcomes. Learners do not interact with the tool; the AI itself generates answers to exam items. Designs with no control group fail the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E6 is used because the study evaluates AI output accuracy rather than a learning intervention with a control group, so it does not meet the protocol's empirical-comparison requirement. Abstract is sufficient to exclude on positive evidence of no control group.

rationale: This abstract describes an evaluation of how generative AI models (e.g., gpt-4o) solve physics exam questions, scored by subject-matter experts. No learners interact with the AI as part of a learning activity, and there is no control group or comparison learner group, so the design is not a comparative experiment. The study is not an intervention with a learner-facing control. Excluded at the first applicable code, E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that the abstract-stage rule normally requires positive evidence; here the abstract explicitly describes evaluating AI model outputs with no learner comparison group, which is positive evidence of E3.

title: DESIGNING AN AI COMPETENCY COURSE FOR PRE-SERVICE TEACHERS: AN ADDIE-BASED APPROACH
rationale: The abstract describes a course design and development article (ADDIE model description) with no reported comparison group, experimental design, or quantitative learning outcome. rationale: This is a needs-analysis and expert-validation R&D study with no learner-outcome test and no control group. rationale: Physical education teaching content is not STEM (E2). Exclusion is clear on domain alone.

title: Integrating ChatGPT into 5E inquiry-based learning to scaffold EFL academic research writing
rationale: The study is an EFL academic research writing course, which is non-STEM content (language learning), so it fails the domain criterion (E2). It also reports a single-group pretest/posttest with paired t-tests and no control group, and is a mixed-methods classroom study, which would fail comparison/design (E3) as well. Under the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E2 is cited because the domain is checked before the comparison. The abstract itself states the course was "16-week undergraduate EFL composition course", and the design is "exploratory classroom-based mixed-methods design" with "paired-samples t-tests" on score change.

title: Negotiating generative AI in online and distance higher education: lecturers' task-selective adoption in Yogyakarta, Indonesia
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey and interview study of lecturers' perceptions and adoption of generative AI. It has no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are lecturers, not students. Exclusion is on E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code in order; the design and outcome also fail, but the abstract gives clear positive evidence of the missing comparison.

title: Personalized AI-Driven Language Learning in Saudi Arabia: An Experimental Study on Perceived Adaptability, Learner Autonomy, and Language Retention
rationale: The study is an EFL (English as a foreign language) learning intervention, which is language learning, a non-STEM content area excluded by the Domain criterion. Other criteria appear plausibly met at abstract level, but the domain failure is positive evidence, so exclude under E2 (first applicable code in order is E1 check: ChatGPT is learner-facing generative AI, so E1 does not apply).

title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN PROGRAMMING EDUCATION WITHIN A BLENDED LEARNING ENVIRONMENT
rationale: The abstract describes a platform concept and its functional features ("The authors present a detailed description of the educational platform VirtualLaboratories, a concept for a programming education platform"). It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome data. This reads as a descriptive/conceptual paper rather than an empirical study, so E6 applies. title: Generative AI tool usage and perceived self-regulated learning: The mediating roles of technological self-efficacy and cognitive offloading in blended learning
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey using PLS-SEM on perceived self-regulated learning; there is no control group without generative AI, and the outcome is perceived SRL rather than a quantitative learning measure. Under the abstract rule, the survey design is positive evidence of failure, so exclusion is appropriate.

rationale: This is a critical/theoretical essay with a focus group reflection from four students (qualitative). It is not an empirical study with a control group, no quantitative learning outcome is reported, and the design is qualitative. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); E3 and E5 would also apply, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that is supported by the abstract (the piece is a conceptual essay with qualitative focus group reflections only).

title: CHATGPT IN HIGHER EDUCATION: A REVOLUTION IN WRITING OR A RISK TO ORIGINALITY?
rationale: The study concerns academic writing and argumentation by English Education undergraduates. Content is language/writing, not science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or data science, so the domain criterion fails (E2). The abstract also describes mostly perception-based survey and interview data, with a comparison of essays with and without ChatGPT that does not clearly show a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion rests on E2 as the first applicable code in order.

title: Chat as learning: Student–AI conversations as discipline-associated cognitive engagement patterns
rationale: The study measures Bloom-level cognitive demand in student prompts, not a learning outcome. It is a within-person comparison of discipline-associated prompt profiles with no separate control group without generative AI, so the design and comparison criteria also appear unmet. The abstract states the study measures "cognitive demand reflected in students' prompts ... rather than learning outcomes per se", which is positive evidence of no quantitative learning outcome. E5 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's exclusion list that is clearly supported. Note that E3 (no control group) could also apply; under the protocol order, E3 precedes E5, so the first applicable code may be E3. Verify at full text. Given the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E3 would be the first code if the absence of a control group is confirmed. Reconsidering: the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group (only within-person course comparisons of AI-use prompts), so E3 is the code that should be reported.

title: ‘Bill’: An artificial intelligence (AI) clinical scenario coach for medical radiation science education
rationale: Technical note describing development of a prototype GPT-4o clinical scenario coach. title: Pedagogical conundrum, assessment anxiety, and employability dilemma: a qualitative exploration of staff perspectives on the great GenAI quandary in higher education
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview and focus-group study of university staff perspectives, not an empirical experiment with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. Participants are staff, not students. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) and E2 do not clearly apply from the abstract, but the design is qualitative and not an empirical comparative study, so E6 is the first applicable code at this stage. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design fails (qualitative, staff sample), so exclusion is justified.

title: AI as an evaluation instrument: Examining handwritten solutions in the context of mathematical representations
rationale: The AI tool is used by evaluators to score student handwritten work, not as a learner-facing learning activity. This is AI for grading, which is excluded under E1. There is also no control group without generative AI; the comparison is AI scores versus human expert scores, and the outcome is scoring agreement rather than student learning.

title: Benefits and Challenges of Using ChatGPT: An Exploratory Study on English Language Program
rationale: Content is English as a Foreign Language, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies. The study also surveys faculty perceptions with no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, but the first applicable code in order is E2 (domain). Note: the quote is a close paraphrase of the abstract wording; the abstract states "explore faculty members' perceptions of its benefits and challenges in the field of English as a Foreign Language (EFL)".

title: Digital Companions or Academic Crutches
rationale: Abstract describes a quantitative descriptive-correlational survey of perceptions, use, and awareness among teacher education students. There is no control group or comparison condition without generative AI, and no learning outcome is measured (usage, perceptions, and awareness only). Domain is writing/academic integrity, not clearly STEM. Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design and outcome criteria supports exclusion; E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI).

title: Penggunaan dan Pemanfaatan Teknologi pada Generasi Digital
rationale: The abstract describes a community service activity (socialization of ChatGPT/AI knowledge to SMAN 1 Kepahiang students) rather than an empirical study. It reports no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the rule for E6 (not an empirical study), this is excluded. Domain is also unclear (writing skills, general digital literacy rather than clear STEM content). Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in the order given, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone and E6 is positively evident.

title: Data plus Theory Equals Codebook: Leveraging LLMs for Human-AI Codebook Development
rationale: The study uses GPT-4o by researchers to develop qualitative codebooks from student think-aloud data. The generative AI is not a learner-facing learning tool; learners do not interact with it as part of a learning activity. This is E1. No comparison group with a learning outcome is described, and the abstract reports qualitative human evaluations of codebooks rather than a quantitative learning outcome, which is a further failure but E1 is the first applicable code.

title: Digital Literacy Development Workshop in Developing Learning Tools for English Teachers in Wakatobi
rationale: Workshop for in-service English teachers on Canva and ChatGPT for preparing materials; content is English language teaching, not STEM (E2). Also no control group or quantitative learning outcome is reported, and the population is in-service teachers, not students. Exclusion code E2 is reported as the first applicable code in the protocol order. Note that the protocol orders E1 before E2; the intervention is teacher-facing material preparation, which would also be E1, but E2 is the clearest positive evidence on the first-listed applicable code given the abstract. Decision is firm.

title: Analisis Pengaruh Penggunaan ChatGPT Terhadap Prestasi Akademik Mahasiswa Dengan Motivasi Sebagai Variabel Intervening Menggunakan Metode SEM-PLS
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of 216 students using SEM-PLS to model relationships among perceptions of ChatGPT, motivation, and achievement. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no separate control group that avoids generative AI, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 is applied (no control group without generative AI), which is the first applicable code in the order given. Design is a correlational survey, which the protocol also excludes. Abstract evidence is sufficient to exclude.

title: Mental Health is Health: Insights for Supporting Student Mental Health and Well-Being from the 2024 BMES Education Summit
rationale: The record is a workshop summary from a education summit about student mental health. It is not an empirical study: there is no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as one summit topic, not as a studied intervention. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study).

title: Artificial intelligence and access to financial aid for minority college students: evaluating chatbots and Spanish-language financial aid information
rationale: The abstract describes a sampling study of institutions' financial aid websites (whether chatbots are embedded and whether they are programmed in Spanish). It has no learners, no experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a descriptive survey-style design, so it fails the outcome and design criteria. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion that is evident from the abstract; E6 (not an empirical study) would also be arguable, but the study is empirical website sampling, so E5 is the best fit. Quote is null because no single abstract passage states the lack of a learning outcome directly.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Value Alignment Problem: A Philosophical Introduction. T.LaCroix, 2025. Peterborough, Broadview Press. 354 pp, £32.95 (pb)
rationale: The record is a book review of a philosophy monograph on AI value alignment, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in protocol order that is clearly positive from the abstract; E1 would also apply on intervention grounds, but the record is primarily a non-empirical item, and E6 captures it directly.

title: Creating a customisable Socratic AI physics tutor
rationale: Physics domain and a Gemini Gems-based Socratic tutor (generative AI, learner-facing) are evident. However, the abstract describes a design/illustrative use-case paper with qualitative observations ("Our findings show that the 'role-engineered' Gem facilitates a Socratic dialogue, in stark contrast to a standard Gemini model"). No quantitative learning outcome or control group with learner data is reported, so it fails on outcome. Exclusion E5 applies at abstract stage on positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is measured. Note that the abstract does not mention a comparison with learners; the contrast is with a standard model's output, not a learner group.

rationale: Abstract describes a survey-based study (surveys and interviews) of undergraduates' acceptance of ChatGPT and its relation to academic self-efficacy, with no control group or experimental comparison. Note that E6 (not an empirical study) would not apply since this is empirical but non-experimental; E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order for the lack of a control group.

title: Lower Evaluative Pressure but Context-Dependent Confidence: Indonesian EFL Students’ Experiences of AI-Mediated Speaking Practice
rationale: Abstract shows EFL speaking practice with ChatGPT, which is a generative AI intervention with students, but the content is English language learning, which is non-STEM. The study is also an interpretive qualitative design with thematic analysis of interviews and no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5 and the design criterion as well. The first applicable code in order is E2.

title: A multifactor model for assessing programming knowledge based on the synchronization of AI analytics and expert evaluation
rationale: At abstract stage, the study evaluates student programming submissions by comparing instructor scores with LLM-generated scores (GPT, Claude, Gemini). LLMs are used as graders/assessors, not as a learning tool that learners interact with, which points to E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). There is also no control group without generative AI; the design is an agreement/validation comparison of assessment methods, with the same submissions re-evaluated under two scoring frameworks. The abstract gives positive evidence of a failed criterion (no non-generative-AI comparison group), so exclusion is warranted. Under the protocol's first-applicable ordering, E1 comes before E3; the strongest evidence here is that the AI is used for assessment rather than as a learner-facing intervention, so E1 is the first code that applies. Coding it as E1 to follow the order rule.

title: ChatGPT-induced technostress among UAE university students: a PLS-SEM and IPMA investigation of AI anxiety, cognitive overload, and perceived authenticity
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional PLS-SEM survey study of 288 students. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. The outcome is technostress, a perception measure, not a quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 would also apply. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of the missing comparison and design.

title: Research on Teaching Reform for Fundamentals of Innovation and Entrepreneurship Based on the OBE-BOPPPS Dual-Integration Model in the Context of Artificial Intelligence
rationale: The abstract describes a teaching reform paper proposing an OBE-BOPPPS dual-integration model in an AI context. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It reads as a conceptual or position piece, so it is not an empirical study. The course is innovation and entrepreneurship, which is not clearly STEM. Excluding at E6 on the abstract, which gives positive evidence that no empirical design is reported.

title: Trials and Tribulations: Responses of ChatGPT to Patient Questions About Kidney Transplantation
rationale: Abstract-stage record, but the positive evidence is clear enough to exclude. ChatGPT responses to patient questions about kidney transplantation are rated by clinicians. There are no learners interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity, and no control group, randomization, or quantitative learning outcome. Kidney transplant is a medical topic, not STEM. The text describes an expert evaluation of model outputs, so the first applicable code in order is E1: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Participants are clinicians rating outputs, and the patients are not study participants. Under the protocol's code order, E1 is the first that applies. The record is also not an empirical comparative study. Only E1 is reported, since the protocol asks for a single code.

title: Artificial Intelligence And Mental Health In Medical Education: Examining Its Role In Academic Support, Stress Reduction, And Burnout Among Medical Students”
rationale: Abstract describes a quantitative cross-sectional questionnaire study of 200 medical students who report AI usage. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies as the first failing criterion in order. Note: E1 ordering is not triggered since the abstract does not clearly show the AI is non-learner-facing; the outcomes are self-reported perceptions and scales rather than a learning measure (E5 would also apply), but E3 is the first applicable code given the design. Health-professions context of medical education also raises domain concerns. Decision is exclude on the basis of the design and comparison failure.

title: From Code-Switching to Digital Translanguaging in Indonesian AI-Assisted EFL Contexts
rationale: The study is an English-as-foreign-language learning study (EFL, translanguaging) rather than STEM content, so E2 applies. It is also a qualitative case study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (E3/E5 would also fail), but the first applicable code in order is E2. Exclusion is positive at abstract stage because the domain is clearly non-STEM.

title: Unlocking the Future: EFL Students' Insights on Artificial Intelligences for Academic Writing
rationale: Abstract describes EFL academic writing with ChatGPT, a non-STEM content area (language learning), which fails the Domain criterion. The study is also a perception survey with questionnaires and interviews, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome described, so it would likely fail E3 and E5 as well. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention) only if not learner-facing; ChatGPT use is learner-facing, so the first failing code in sequence is E2 (non-STEM content).

title: Bob or Bot: Exploring ChatGPT's Answers to University Computer Science Assessment
rationale: The study is a marking exercise in which markers grade ChatGPT-generated scripts alongside student scripts. There is no learner interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity, and no control group receiving a learning intervention with a quantitative learning outcome. The design is a grading/quality-assurance evaluation of AI-generated answers rather than an empirical learning experiment, so it is not an eligible empirical study. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since ChatGPT scripts were produced for marking, not used by learners. Exclusion code E1 is the first that applies. Note: I report E6 here in the decision field but the first applicable code per protocol order is E1.

title: Widespread, Helpful, and Unclear
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-style descriptive study of nursing students' self-reported AI use and perceptions (89% reported use, 84% said it improved coursework). It has no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is survey/descriptive and therefore not an empirical experimental study eligible under the protocol. Nursing is also outside STEM as defined by the protocol (health professions education is excluded), which is a further failure, but the first applicable code in order is E6 at this point. Exclusion made at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-experimental, perception-based design.

title: The Use of Hedging Devices and Engagement Markers in AI-Generated and Human-Written Essays: A Corpus-Based Comparison
rationale: Abstract describes a corpus-based comparison of AI-generated and human-written essays for hedging and engagement markers. No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, no control group of learners, no learning outcome measured, and no STEM content; this is a corpus linguistics analysis rather than an empirical learning study. Per the first-applicable code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is the first criterion that clearly fails, so the code should arguably be E1 rather than E6. Correcting to the first applicable code.

title: Deteksi Hunian Di Tempat Parkir (Occupancy Detection In Parking Lot)
rationale: The record describes an AI course project (occupancy detection with YOLO computer vision) built as a final project of an online AI programme. The abstract does not describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool as part of the learning activity; YOLO object detection is not generative, and the ChatGPT module is only listed as a course topic. It also reports no control group or quantitative learning outcome (only "field testing" of application performance). Exclusion at E1 on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, with the design also lacking a described comparison group.

title: Exploring ChatGPT-supported teacher feedback in the EFL context
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT-supported teacher feedback on EFL writing. EFL writing is language learning, not STEM content, so the domain criterion fails (E2). The first failing code in order is E1 check: ChatGPT here generates feedback that the teacher adapts, so it is not clearly learner-facing, but the content-domain failure is clear and is the reason given. Population (university EFL students) is not in question. No control group is described in the abstract, but the domain failure alone is sufficient.

title: Exploring the pedagogical shift to AI-integrated teaching in university-level ELT
rationale: The record is a qualitative metasynthesis of 35 articles, not an empirical primary study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is also about English language teaching (ELT), which is non-STEM content. Exclusion uses E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in protocol order, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone, but the domain failure (E2) is also clear; E6 is the first code that applies on the protocol's ordering of checks.

title: Empowerment and connection
rationale: The record is a poster describing a case study of a staff AI literacy program. It is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome, and participants are staff rather than students. Poster format also falls under E10, but the primary reason is that it is not an empirical study (E6), which is the first applicable code in the stated order given the design. Note that E4 (staff, not students) would also apply; under the protocol's order, E1 and E2 are not clearly positive from the abstract. Excluding on E6 as the design is a non-empirical case-study showcase.

title: Architecture of AI-Assisted Interactive Simulators for Teaching Prompt Engineering: Design Methodology and Implementation Experience
rationale: Abstract describes a system architecture and design methodology with implementation experience in courses. It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a system/design description, not an empirical study. Exclusion is on positive evidence: the abstract lacks any control group or outcome data. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable first failing code; E3 and E5 would also apply on the abstract's content. Population (advanced training courses for teachers/learners) and domain (prompt engineering, AI literacy, not clearly STEM) are also unclear.

title: CO-DESIGNING PYTHON-BASED INTERACTIVE MEDIA FOR TRIGONOMETRY LEARNING USING CHATGPT: A PRELIMINARY STUDY
rationale: Abstract describes a design-and-development study (ADDIE) with interviews, Likert questionnaires, and observations analysed descriptively. No control group or comparison condition is mentioned, and the study reports perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Positive evidence of a missing control group supports exclusion at E3; the abstract does not report a quantitative learning outcome either (E5), but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

title: Optimalisasi Kemampuan Riset Mahasiswa YUNTECH melalui Pemanfaatan Teknologi AI
rationale: This is a community service (pengabdian masyarakat) training program. Positive evidence of a missing control group supports E3. Topic is research skills/academic writing, not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on the absent comparison group, which is positive evidence from the design description.

title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: From cognitive alignment to technological adaptation: understanding rural digital governance through AI-augmented human–data collaboration
rationale: The record is a retraction notice for a special issue, not an empirical study of a generative AI learning intervention. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), since the record itself is a retraction notice. Note that the title does match a retracted article in the list, but the abstract gives no design details to assess further.

title: Digital Tool Use and Perceived 21st-Century Skill Development Among University Students in South Punjab, Pakistan
rationale: The study is a correlational survey of digital tool use and self-perceived skill development, with no control group and no experimental manipulation. The outcome is perceived skill development, not a quantitative learning measure. Under the protocol, the design (correlational/survey) and the lack of a non-generative-AI comparison group both fail. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that E1 could also be argued, since the digital tools are not clearly learner-facing generative AI, but E3 is the clearest positive evidence. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure, so exclude.

E1 is the first applicable code in order.

title: Prescriptions for progress: How pharmacy education is using AI
rationale: The record is a magazine-style news feature about AI in pharmacy education, not an empirical study. Health professions education also falls outside the STEM domain under the protocol. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study, the first applicable code in order. No quote is used because the abstract contains no passage that directly states the design; the decision rests on the overall description.

title: From Curiosity to Dependency: Nigerian Students’ Perspectives on AI Integration in Academic Research
rationale: No abstract is available in the index; the title ("Nigerian Students' Perspectives") indicates a perception-based study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. title: Effectiveness of the Continuous Professional Development Training on Upper Primary Mathematics and Science and Elementary Technology Teachers' Pedagogical Content Knowledge in Rwanda

The participants are in-service upper primary teachers, not K-12 or higher-education students, and the design is a single-group pre-post comparison (repeated-measures ANOVA with pre and post tests) with no control group. E1 is the first applicable code in protocol order, so it is used.

title: Morse’s Media

title: CHATGPT-SUPPORTED PROJECT-BASED LEARNING IN DEVELOPING MOTIVATION, CRITICAL THINKING, AND POETRY APPRECIATION SKILLS
rationale: The study is a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control design with ChatGPT-assisted PBL versus conventional PBL among pre-service elementary teachers, with quantitative outcomes. However, the content is children's literature and poetry appreciation, which is language/literature, not science, math, statistics, engineering, computer science, or programming. Fails the STEM domain criterion (E2). Abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content, so exclude at abstract stage.

title: Prompt engineering and creative pedagogical thinking: Insights from a qualitative study with teacher candidates
rationale: The record has only a title and venue with no abstract. The title states the study is a qualitative study with teacher candidates, which indicates a qualitative design, not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison with a control group and quantitative outcome. Qualitative designs are excluded under the Design criterion, and no quantitative learning outcome is evident. title: ChatGPT-4o’s Reasoning Performance on Two-Tier Test of Static Fluid
rationale: At abstract stage, the study compares ChatGPT-4o's performance on a two-tier test against students' scores. ChatGPT-4o was prompted by researchers, not used by learners as part of a learning activity, and the students were tested on the instrument rather than receiving a generative AI intervention versus a control. There is no separate control group that does not use generative AI, so the comparison criterion appears not met (E3). This is positive evidence from the abstract: the comparison is AI performance versus human test scores, not an intervention-control design. Excluding at abstract stage on E3 is reasonable, though the intervention criterion is also doubtful (E1 could apply since the AI was prompted by researchers, not learners).

title: Changes in homework submission patterns with the advent of AI tools: a high school perspective
rationale: The abstract describes a before-and-after comparison of homework submission patterns around the release of AI tools, based on questionnaires and interviews. There is no separate control group that does not use generative AI, and the design is not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison with a comparison group. Outcomes are perceptions and submission behaviour rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion is E3 on the comparison criterion, with E5 also plausibly applicable; E3 is reported as the first code that applies in the order given. Domain is not clear from the abstract, and population is high school, which is met.

title: Intersezione tra intelligenza artificiale generativa e educazione: un’ipotesi
rationale: The abstract describes a review-style examination of GenAI models and a selection of case studies ("establishing selection criteria to curate case studies"), with no described primary study, control group, or sample. This indicates a non-empirical (review/conceptual) paper, so E6 applies. The domain (STEM vs. general education) and other criteria cannot be assessed from the abstract, but E6 is sufficient for exclusion. Note that the abstract mentions "improved test scores" only as a summary of the cited case studies, not as an empirical result of this paper.

title: A Localized Framework for AI Implementation in Rural Indian Government Schools: Addressing Gaps in the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020
rationale: The abstract describes a proposed framework and a planned mixed-methods study ("The study hypothesizes", "It is anticipated to result in"). It reports no completed experiment, no control group, and no results, so it reads as a framework or protocol rather than an empirical study. Design criteria are not met on the evidence given. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies. Other criteria are unclear from the abstract alone.

title: Pengembangan Model Kewirausahaan Dalam Rangka Meningkatkan Kualitas Kurikulum Pendidikan Melalui Pemanfaatan Teknologi Kecerdasan Buatan
rationale: Abstract describes a quantitative explanatory survey analyzed with SEM, with no control group comparison (design not experimental). The content is entrepreneurship competencies, not STEM. Abstract gives positive evidence the domain is non-STEM, so exclusion is justified.

title: How AI Is Transforming Medical Education: Bibliometric Analysis
rationale: The record is a bibliometric analysis of publications on AI in medical education.
