Stated as the basis: this is a review/perspective article, not an empirical study. Title and abstract are not an abstract in the usual sense; the text is a long discursive passage. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on the basis that the record gives positive evidence of a non-empirical article.

title: PENGARUH AI GEMINI TERHADAP SELF-EFFICACY MATEMATIS SISWA SMK
rationale: The only outcome is mathematical self-efficacy measured by a Likert questionnaire. Self-efficacy is a perception/affective measure, not a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement, conceptual knowledge, problem solving, or skill performance. Protocol says affective outcomes are not extracted, so E5 applies. Other criteria appear met at abstract stage (AI Gemini in math learning, posttest-only control group, vocational high school students, 2026 publication, journal). Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the outcome fails.

title: Developing learning-strategic competence in pre-service Еnglish teachers through artificial intelligence tools
rationale: The study concerns English language learning strategies for pre-service English teachers, which is language learning and non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract describes a theoretically developed model with no indication of a controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Domain failure is the first applicable code in order.

title: The Use of Prompt Engineering in Creating Mathematical Modelling Activities with Artificial Intelligence Tool ChatGPT
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT generating mathematical modelling activities from prompt formats, with researchers evaluating outputs against design principles. No learners interact with the tool, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. The study is a qualitative content analysis of generated outputs, so it is not an empirical study of learning. Exclusion at E6 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly evidenced; E1 (learner-facing requirement) is also likely applicable, but the abstract shows the tool used by teachers/researchers for design, which under the borderline rule maps to E1. Given code order, E1 takes precedence over E6 when the tool is teacher-only.

title: A Case Study of AI Agent–Assisted Correction of Intermediate-Level Chinese Writing
rationale: The AI agent is used for automated scoring of essays; learners do not interact with it as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). Also the design is an agreement/correlation study between AI and human raters with no control group without generative AI (E3 would also apply), and the domain is Chinese language learning, which is non-STEM (E2). Under the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E1 is given.

title: Impacto de la aplicación de una intervención didáctica con Chat GPT en las percepciones de los estudiantes de medicina
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group quasi-experimental pre-post design measuring only perceptions (confidence, general impact, willingness to recommend). The protocol excludes single-group pre-post designs (E3) and outcomes limited to perceptions (E5). Reporting only perceptions with no quantitative learning outcome is the clearest positive failure. Domain is physiology, which is health professions education and so also falls outside the protocol's domain scope. The first applicable code in the order is E1 only if intervention fails; ChatGPT as a learner-facing tool is met, so E3 comes before E5 in the sequence. Because the rule asks for the first code in order, the design failure (no separate control group, E3) is the code that applies first here. Note the domain issue (medical physiology, health professions) is also a fail, but the protocol's code list puts E2 (non-STEM) earlier than E3; physiology in medicine is health sciences, which the protocol excludes under Domain.

title: Accuracy and Creativity Analysis of ChatGPT in Quantitative Aptitude
rationale: ChatGPT is used to generate quantitative aptitude questions and human specialists rate their accuracy and creativity. Learners do not interact with the tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). There is no control group without generative AI and no learning outcome in students. The study evaluates AI output quality, not learning. Excluded at the first applicable code, E1.

title: Pemanfaatan Literasi Digital dan Etika Penggunaan Kecerdasan Buatan Generatif di Kalangan Pelajar
rationale: Community service activity with a single group evaluated by pre-test and post-test before and after training, with no separate control group. The protocol excludes single-group pre-post designs (E3). Population (senior high school students) and the generative AI focus appear compatible, and domain is unclear as the content is digital literacy and ethics rather than STEM. The E3 code applies on the design/comparison failure, which is sufficient for exclusion.

title: Implementing AI Course Assistants: A Rapid Design Case from Concept to Full Rollout at Los Angeles Pacific University
rationale: The record is a design case describing an institutional rollout. It reports no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome data. Its own self-description is a design case, not an empirical comparative study, so E6 applies. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design criterion and the outcome criterion fail, so exclusion is justified even under the abstract-stage rule.

title: Implicaciones éticas del uso de Inteligencia Artificial en educación superior
rationale: The abstract describes a systematic literature review plus a survey of university students about attitudes and ethical perceptions toward ChatGPT. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is survey-based, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Not an empirical learning study, so E6 applies at the first failing point in order is actually E3 (no control group) for design-level reasons; however, the survey-only, perception-based design is most directly non-empirical-for-learning. Coded E6 as the best fit; the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group and no learning outcome, so exclusion is supported.

title: AI-augmented supervision in shared chat spaces: how transparent, collaborative engagement with generative AI supports domain-specific critical engagement in project-based learning
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative-dominant two-phase mixed-methods study with no control or comparison group; outcomes are transcript-coded dialogue moves, revision counts, and survey perceptions, with no quantitative learning outcome or comparison. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3 (no control group without generative AI). Domain is business/AI course, which is not clearly STEM, but the comparison failure is the primary basis. Exclusion is based on the abstract's design description.

title: Human Reliability vs. Machine Consistency: Evaluating AI-Based Grading in Language Education
rationale: Title indicates AI-based grading in language education. Language learning is explicitly excluded from the STEM domain criterion, so E2 applies. Also, AI used only for grading would fail the intervention criterion (E1), but E2 is the first applicable code in the stated order only if ordered earlier; E1 precedes E2 in the protocol. Note: under strict code order, AI used only for grading is not learner-facing generative AI (E1) and should be considered first. The record is excluded on the basis of the evident non-STEM content with no abstract available to confirm other criteria. The abstract is not available, so this decision rests on the title alone and should be verified at full text if the reviewer disagrees.

title: Explaining Generative AI Acceptance Among Pre-Service Informatics Teachers: An Extended UTAUT2 Perspective
LLM-GAIによる日本語教材の開発——精読用テキストの自動生成と評価を中心に——
rationale: The study concerns Japanese language teaching materials generated by LLM-based GAI, with topics of pop culture (idols, fashion, manga). Japanese language learning is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also reports evaluation of text quality (difficulty, accuracy) rather than a learning outcome in a controlled comparison, and no control group is described. Only the first applicable code is reported, which is E2.

title: Trusting AI to detect AI? A systematic evaluation of the reliability and robustness of current AIGC detection tools for student academic work
rationale: The study evaluates AIGC detection tools' accuracy on student work; learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. This is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). It also has no control group with a learning outcome and no SMD-type data, so it would fail E3 and E5 as well, but E1 is the first applicable code in order. Abstract evidence is sufficient for exclusion.

title: Investigating the factors influencing the adoption and use of artificial intelligence applications among Pakistani university research scholars: An empirical study
rationale: Survey-based study (questionnaire of 235 research scholars, regression of behavioral intention). No experimental or comparison-group design, and the outcome is behavioral intention/adoption perception rather than a quantitative learning measure. Excluded at the first applicable code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the design also fails the comparison and design criteria, but the rule is to report the first code that applies in order. Note: the rule order places E3 before E5 for comparison failure; however, the outcome failure is clear from the abstract. Abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no learning outcome.

title: The EE-AID Model: An Instructional Design Process Integrating Ethics into the AI-TPACK Framework for University Lecturers
rationale: The paper is a conceptual/theoretical proposal of an instructional design process (EE-AID) for lecturers, built through conceptual analysis and theoretical synthesis. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Population is university lecturers (in-service teachers), which also falls outside the protocol. Exclusion at E6 is the first applicable code in the order that fits the abstract's positive evidence.

title: Artificial Intelligence in scientific publications?
rationale: The record is an opinion/editorial-style piece on AI in scientific publishing and ChatGPT's societal implications. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Under the abstract rule, the exclusion rests on the abstract describing a discussion piece rather than an empirical design. No passage gives a verbatim quote for the non-empirical nature beyond the general framing, so quote is null.

title: Development of a data mining methodology for an analytical system supporting students’ professional development
rationale: Abstract describes a methodology and architecture for GPT-4-based competency matching and gap analysis over academic programs, job vacancies, and 286 students' documents. It reports no control group or comparison condition without generative AI, and no learning outcome measured in learners. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports exclusion at E3. The intervention is also not clearly learner-facing (GPT-4 processes documents for analysis), but the comparison failure is the clearest ground. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported because the abstract lacks any control arm.

title: Goliath and the Cognitive Load Theory
rationale: The abstract describes a tool (Goliath) for educators to generate programming exercises, with AI support, and a set of CLT-based guidelines for template creation. Learners do not interact with the tool; it is used by educators to create materials, which is E1-type. However, the rule to use E1 is for AI used only by teacher to prepare materials, and the protocol says report the first code that applies in order, with E1 first. Since the abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is teacher-facing material preparation, E1 would be the first applicable code. The article also has no comparison group, no learning outcome, and is a tool/guidelines description rather than an empirical learner study, so E6 is also plausible. Following the code order, the first applicable code is E1.

title: Between support and substitution: the impact of artificial intelligence use on anxiety and learning performance among Spanish majors in China
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of 733 Spanish majors with factor analysis, correlations, and regressions on self-reported AI usage behaviors. There is no randomized or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first positive failure at abstract stage, with E3 chosen because no control group exists. Domain is unclear (Spanish language learning is not STEM, which would be a stronger exclusion), but that is not needed given the design failure.

title: Approaches to the application of artificial intelligence in educational activities
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical analysis and systematization of approaches, not an empirical study. No control group, design, or quantitative learning outcome is reported. This is a non-empirical article, so E6 applies. Exclusion is justified on positive evidence from the abstract itself.

title: Cover and Table of Content
rationale: This record is the front matter (cover, foreword, and table of contents) of a journal issue, not a research article. It reports no study design, comparison group, or outcome data. The foreword mentions an article on ChatGPT and HOTS problems, but that is a separate item whose design and data cannot be assessed from this record. Under E6 (not an empirical study), the record itself is not eligible. Note that the ChatGPT article listed in the foreword ("Mathematics in the AI Era: The Effectiveness of ChatGPT in Helping Students Solve HOTS Problems") may warrant separate screening on its own full text.

title: PENGARUH FAKTOR PSIKOLOGIS DALAM THEORY OF PLANNED BEHAVIOR (TPB) TERHADAP PERILAKU BERPIKIR KRITIS MAHASISWA PAP UNESA DI ERA DIGITAL
rationale: This is a correlational PLS-SEM survey study of TPB psychological factors. No learner interaction with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity is described; generative AI is mentioned only as a background concern. No experimental control group exists, and the design is survey-based, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Excluded at E1 as the first applicable code (no learner-facing generative AI intervention). Other criteria are also not met (survey design, no control group), but E1 is the first code in order.

title: Interactivity as a key element in distance English learning under martial law: A case study
rationale: Content is English language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM (E2). The study also reads as a mixed-methods case study with active vs passive user comparisons and surveys, with no generative AI intervention described (interactive tools such as Kahoot and Quizlet Live are not generative AI). E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order. Quote is from the title and abstract; the cited phrase is the title's description of the content, not a verbatim statement of a STEM exclusion.

title: AI-INDUCED ACADEMIC DEVIANCE: A CRIMINOLOGICAL STUDY ON CHANGES IN STUDENTS’ LIFE ACTIVITIES AND CONDUCT
rationale: Survey-style quantitative study of criminology students' AI use and perceptions. No control group without generative AI is described, and outcomes are self-reported perceptions and attitudes (study habits, ethics, integrity) rather than a quantitative learning measure. Criminology is not STEM. Exclusion coded E3 for lack of a comparison group, which is the most evident failure; the STEM-domain and outcome failures also apply. Abstract-stage evidence is positive for the missing control group and non-STEM content.

title: The Logical Reasoning, Value Implications and Practical Path of Generative AI Technology Empowering the Teaching of Civics and Politics Classes in Colleges and Universities
rationale: The abstract is a theoretical/discursive paper ("systematically explores its logical rationale, value implication and practical path") with no described empirical design, control group, or quantitative outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies as the first failing criterion in code order. Domain (civics and politics, an ideological course) is also not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that the paper is non-empirical.

title: PENGARUH PENGGUNAAN AI GENERATIF SEBAGAI ASISTEN BELAJAR TERHADAP LITERASI DIGITAL KRITIS MAHASISWA TEKNIK INFORMATIKA
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group without generative AI, which is the E3 exclusion (single-group pre-post). Domain is also unclear: critical digital literacy is not clearly STEM content, but E3 applies first in the order given the design failure. Population (university informatics students) and outcome (questionnaire score) appear to be met.

title: Extraction of Knowledge Models from Textbooks
rationale: The record is a column-style newsletter piece (ACM SIGWEB Newsletter) with a author biography rather than an abstract. It describes no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under E1 the intervention is also not described; E6 is the first code that clearly applies in the protocol order for a non-empirical item.

title: ChatGPT Without a Safety Net
rationale: The record is an editorial/commentary on generative AI detectors in nursing education. It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no learning outcome data. The abstract itself describes a discussion piece on AI detection, accuracy, and academic integrity. Under E6 (not an empirical study) it is excluded. E1 was considered first, but the abstract does not describe a learner-facing AI intervention in a study, so the first applicable code is taken as E6 by order-of-evidence; the main failure is non-empirical design.

title: Theoretical Framework for an AI-Enhanced Pedagogical Technology to Develop Self-Editing Skills of Doctoral Students
rationale: The abstract describes an integrative literature review and a theoretical framework design, with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Domain (writing/self-editing) is also not clearly STEM. E6 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's checks that is clearly supported; E1/E2 are not clearly established from the abstract alone, so E6 is applied.

title: Technology-Integrated Teaching in Higher Education: An Empirical Study on AI-Supported Learning, Digital Tools, and LMS Innovations
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of 320 students measuring perceived usefulness, satisfaction, and self-perceived learning outcomes, with correlation and regression analyses. There is no control group and no experimental design, and the learning outcome is perceived rather than a quantitative measure of achievement. The abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with perception-based outcomes, so it is excluded. E5 is applied because the outcome is perceptual; the design (no comparison group, survey) would also fail E3 and the design criterion. Domain is unclear since STEM content is not specified.

title: An Empirical Study of Artificial Intelligence Use in English for Specific Purposes (ESP): A Case of English-Major Students at Trade Union University
rationale: Exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence. The study is an English for Specific Purposes (ESP) study, which is language learning and non-STEM content, so E2 applies first in the code order. The abstract also describes a descriptive survey with Likert questionnaires and open-ended questions, with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome, which would support E3 and E5 as well. E2 is reported as the first applicable code.

title: Investigating the Security Risks of Gen-AI-Powered Phishing Attacks on University Students
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional online survey (N=63) using a simulated GenAI phishing email as a stimulus. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the design is survey-based rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment. Domain (cybersecurity/phishing awareness) is not clearly a protocol STEM domain, and the outcomes are self-reported confidence and likelihood to click rather than a learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is the first clear failure in order of the code list; the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group.

title: Workshop Pengembangan Media Pembelajaran Interaktif Kimia menggunakan Canva dan ChatGPT
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pretest-posttest pre-experimental design with no separate control group, which is positive evidence of failure on the comparison and design criteria (E3). The participants are in-service chemistry teachers, not students, which also fails the population criterion (E4). Either way the record is excluded; E3 is reported as the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol.

title: Conversational Implicature in Chatbot Interactions: A Relevance Theory Study among University Students in Lahore
rationale: The study is a qualitative pragmatics study (elicited transcripts and semi-structured interviews, relevance-theoretic coding). It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the content is linguistic pragmatics, not STEM. It is not an empirical comparison design eligible under the protocol. Excluded under E6 as a qualitative, non-experimental study; the E6 code is the first applicable one in order after checking E1 (intervention is generative AI chatbot use, so E1 is not clearly met).

title: Comparative analysis of NLP-driven MCQ generators from text sources
rationale: The study benchmarks AI tools' ability to generate MCQs from text against a common dataset. It is a tool comparison with no learners interacting with the tool and no control group of learners. No quantitative learning outcome in learners is reported; the outcomes are tool performance metrics. Exclusion at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the best-fitting code, though E1 (learner-facing intervention) could also apply since the AI is used to generate assessment items rather than as a learner-facing tool. The abstract gives positive evidence that no learner outcome is measured, so exclude.

title: Enhancing Higher Education with Generative AI: A Multimodal Approach for Personalised Learning
rationale: The abstract describes design and development of a multimodal chatbot demonstrated as a practical web application. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the evaluation is of sentiment analysis and course evaluation summaries. This is a system description rather than an empirical study with a control group. Excluded at the abstract stage on E6 (not an empirical study), since the abstract gives positive evidence of no controlled empirical design. STEM domain and student population are not stated in the abstract.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MENTAL HEALTH EDUCATION IN JUNIOR SECONDARY SCHOOLS, NYAMIRA COUNTY
rationale: The study concerns AI-facilitated mental health screening in junior secondary schools, which is not STEM content (E2). Code E2 is first in order that applies, since E1 (learner-facing generative AI) is unclear from the abstract. The abstract also reports pre/post screening rates without a described control group, which points to E3 as well, but the domain failure is the clearest positive evidence. No quote from the abstract explicitly states a control group or a generative model, so the quote is null for the decision.

title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence in Informatics and Information Technology Education
rationale: The abstract describes a methodological/practice piece presenting a didactic framework, with no description of an empirical comparison, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. It appears not to be an empirical study (E6). Informatics/IT education would fall within STEM, and the generative AI component is met, but the design is not described as an experiment or quasi-experiment. Excluding under E6 on positive evidence that no empirical design is reported.

title: Human–AI Feedback Synergy Assessing the Reliability and Contextual Depth of Generative Evaluation Systems in Enterprise-Scale Education
rationale: Study compares GPT-4 generated feedback with human assessors on typography projects in a Visual Media program, which is creative design rather than STEM. It is also a mixed-methods evaluation of feedback quality and perceptions, with no clear learner-facing learning outcome or control-group experimental design described in the abstract. Excluded on E2 (content not STEM), the first applicable code in order.

title: Neural-Symbolic AI System
rationale: The abstract describes a benchmark of AI architectures evaluated on AI reasoning datasets (CLEVR, FOLIO, FB15k-237, HumanEval, etc.). It reports no learners, no human learning intervention, and no control group with a learning outcome. There is positive evidence that the design is a computational benchmark rather than an empirical study of learners, so E6 applies. Other criteria cannot be assessed from the abstract. Note that the record is a benchmark, not a learner-facing study, so the first-applicable code could arguably be E1; E6 is chosen because the study is not an empirical learning study at all.

title: Pragmatic Failure in EFL Learners’ Emails and AI Grammar Tools Feedback
rationale: The study concerns EFL learners' academic email pragmatics (requests, apologies, politeness) and AI grammar tool feedback. This is language learning, which the protocol explicitly excludes as non-STEM content. E2 applies. Other criteria are unclear from the abstract, but the domain failure alone is sufficient.

title: Training EFL Pre-Service Teachers in Using AI Tools to Create Digital Narrative Teaching Materials
rationale: Abstract describes EFL (English as a foreign language) material development and language skills, which is non-STEM content (E2). Also, the design appears to be a single-group mixed-methods study with training observations and satisfaction survey, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported, so E3 and E5 would also apply, but the first applicable code in order is E2 under the protocol's sequence. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

title: Artificial Intelligence Enhanced Instruction: Reflection on Teachers and Students’ Perceptions and Practices
rationale: Abstract describes a mixed-methods survey/perception study (questionnaires, focus groups, interviews) of teachers and students at Tanzanian universities. There is no separate control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition and no learning outcome measured after an intervention; the study reports perceptions and practices. Design and comparison are not met, and the outcome is not a learning measure. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in the protocol order after E1/E2 were not clearly triggered; the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design lacking a comparison group.

title: GenAI language corpora in foreign language teaching: advantages and disadvantages
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical literature analysis and conceptual comparison of ChatGPT and corpora technologies, with no empirical design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Domain is foreign language teaching, which is non-STEM (E2) as well, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that is clearly supported. Note the order rule: E1 (intervention) and E2 (content) are checked first; the content is language learning, which is non-STEM, so E2 would arguably apply first. Recording E2 would be the strict order-based code; see the rationale in the decision for auditing.

title: Artificial Intelligence is Changing Your World – Is it Dystopian?
rationale: This is a journal editorial introducing an issue of Advances in Skin & Wound Care, not an empirical study. It reports no controlled comparison, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, and no learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first code that applies in the protocol's order given that the editorial's content is commentary. Wound care is also not STEM, but E6 is reported as the first applicable code.

title: 2023 CASEM Podium Presentations
rationale: This record is a conference abstract compilation (CASEM 2023 podium presentations) covering multiple unrelated sports-medicine studies. None involve learners interacting with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the studies are about wearable activity monitors, MEG imagery, instrumented mouthguards, radiographic outcomes, video analysis, and sleep metrics. Also, the items are non-STEM sports medicine and not controlled learning studies. Publication type is a conference abstract collection (E10 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E1 because the intervention is not generative AI.

title: Impacto axiológico y normativo de la inteligencia artificial generativa en las Maestrías de la Universidad Nacional Rosario Castellanos
rationale: The study is a non-experimental, cross-sectional mixed-methods survey with no control group that lacks generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. Its outcomes are perceptions and dispositions (Likert questionnaire, interviews), not a quantitative learning measure, so E5 would also apply. Per the protocol's order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, and E3 is the first clear failure in the sequence applied here. Design also fails (survey, not experimental or quasi-experimental with a comparison group).

title: How has the pandemic accelerated the transformation of Analytical Chemistry education from Generation Z to Alpha?
rationale: The record is an opinion/experience essay by an instructor. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It has no generative AI learner intervention beyond a closing question about ChatGPT. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code, since E1 would also apply only loosely and the paper is not empirical.

title: Labsense: an Ai Integrated Lab Examination Evaluation System
rationale: The abstract describes a system (LabSense) with an LLM used for grading and anti-cheat features in a coding lab exam. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome data; it reads as a system description rather than an empirical study. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study) on positive evidence from the abstract's descriptive framing, with no quantitative outcome or control group reported. The LLM here is used for evaluating student code (grading), which also raises an E1 concern, but the first applicable code in order is E6 only if the study lacks empirical evidence; the abstract gives no evaluation data, so E6 is the most supported code.

title: PROCTORED ASSESSMENTS TO MITIGATE PLAGIARISM: A DESIGN-BASED RESEARCH STUDY IN PROGRAMMING EDUCATION
rationale: The abstract describes proctored, timed testing as an assessment solution addressing ChatGPT-related plagiarism. Nothing indicates that learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the intervention is an assessment format. It is also a Design-Based Research study without a clearly described control group. Excluded at E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), the first code that applies. Programming domain and master's population are met.

title: Perceived AI – Tools Proficiency and Skill among Higher Education Science Major Students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey (30-item Synthetic Index, descriptive statistics) of students' perceptions and self-rated AI proficiency. There is no control group or experimental comparison, so the design is not an eligible randomized or quasi-experimental design and no control-group comparison exists. Outcomes are perceptions and self-ratings, not a quantitative learning measure. Per the protocol's E3 code (no control group without generative AI), this is excluded. Note that the survey design would also fail the design criterion and the outcome criterion; E3 is reported as the first applicable code in the stated order is E1 (intervention) which is unclear from the abstract, so E3 is used as the most direct failing criterion on positive evidence of no comparison group.

title: Inteligencia artificial en la educación superior: uso y percepción del alumnado de periodismo
rationale: Abstract describes an online questionnaire of 332 journalism students plus a focus group, examining usage and perceptions of generative AI. This is a survey/mixed-methods descriptive design with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and journalism is not STEM. Clear positive evidence that comparison, design, domain and outcome criteria fail. Assigned E6 (not an empirical study is arguable; survey design fails design criterion). Note: the first applicable code in order is E2 (content not STEM), which would be the strictly correct code under the stated order; see rationale-level note.

title: "Relevant but Somewhat Outdated": Children's Librarians' Perspectives on Their Education and Training in the Southeastern United States
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of five children's librarians, which is not an empirical experiment with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI appears only as a topic of needed knowledge. Codes E1 through E5 are arguably also applicable, but the design is qualitative, so E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs) is the best first-applicable code given the order rules; the abstract provides positive evidence that the design is qualitative.

title: Coautores sintéticos: avaliação conceitual de planos de aula em biologia gerados por IAGs
rationale: The abstract describes an expert-rating analysis of 52 AI-generated biology lesson plans. No learners interact with the AI, there is no control group, and no learning outcome is measured. The design is an evaluation of generated artifacts, not an empirical learner study, so it fails the non-empirical/design requirements. Excluded on the first applicable code in order, E1 not clearly applicable since the AI produces plans for teachers, but the teacher-only use maps to E1 as well. Following the protocol's order, the decision is recorded as E6 because the paper is an artifact-rating study rather than an empirical study with learners. The rubric scores are not learning outcomes, and no comparison group is described.

title: COMPARİNG TEACHERS AND CHATGPT İN POSİNG QUALİTY QUESTİONS ON MATTER CYCLES
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative comparative case study comparing teachers' and ChatGPT's question-posing, with no learner-facing intervention, no control group receiving a learning intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are in-service science teachers, not students. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible quantitative design); the design is qualitative and descriptive. Note that the first applicable code in order would arguably be E1 (ChatGPT is not used by learners here, it is only a comparator generating questions), but the clearest failure is design. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure, so exclusion is justified.

Under the protocol, conference proceedings/abstract-only records are publication-type ineligible (E10), but the protocol's E10 code applies to conference proceedings; the record is an abstract collection, so E10 is the most fitting code. Note: the first-applicable code ordering is E1 (intervention not learner-facing genAI) first; the abstracts include a generative AI tool (DiaShield X using ChatGPT-4) used by clinicians, not learners, which is E1 applicable. Choosing E1 as the first applicable code in protocol order.

title: The impact of Gen AI on art and design program education
rationale: Abstract describes Gen AI in art and design education. Art and design is not one of the protocol's STEM domains (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), so the content criterion fails. The abstract also gives no indication of a control group, a learning outcome measure, or a comparative quantitative design, but the domain failure alone is sufficient. Exclude at E2, the first applicable code in order.

title: The Signals That Matter: Resumes, Cover Letters, and Success on the Job Search
rationale: The study observes job applicants' resumes and cover letters and their job-search outcomes. No learner interacts with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; ChatGPT is mentioned only as a speculative future source of document features. Not a learning intervention, not STEM content, and the design is observational rather than an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison with a control group. Excluded at the first applicable code, E1.

title: INVESTIGATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN GENERATING LVAR
rationale: Abstract describes generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Leonardo.AI, Lumen5.AI, Pictory.AI) used to create Linking Visual Active Representations, and an educational experiment. However, the abstract describes content analysis of a ChatGPT dialogue and a qualitative-style evaluation through Bloom's taxonomy; it reports no quantitative learning outcome, no control group, and no effect data. Positive evidence of a missing quantitative outcome is present, so exclusion under E5 is applied. Not clearly STEM either, but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given at abstract stage based on the evidence available. The "experiment" wording is not enough to show a control group or quantitative measure.

title: Investigating pre-service teachers’ AI literacy for ELL instruction: A mixed-methods study
rationale: Study concerns pre-service teachers' AI literacy for ELL (English language learner) instruction, a language-teaching context rather than STEM content. The design appears to be a single-group pre-post comparison ("before and after two interventions"), with no control group described, which would also fail E3. Excluded under E2 as the first applicable code, per the ordering. Quote is null because the abstract supports the content judgment only indirectly.

title: Prevalence of artificial intelligence use and instruction in nursing education: A national study of prelicensure nursing programs in the United States
rationale: The record is a national prevalence study of AI use and instruction in prelicensure nursing programs, which is a survey-type design. It reports no learner-facing intervention with a comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Nursing is also a health professions domain, which the protocol excludes. The abstract is missing, but the title alone indicates a non-experimental prevalence study, so it is excluded as not an empirical intervention study. Exclusion code E6 is used because it is a survey (non-experimental) design, which fails the design criterion. Note that the protocol's domain exclusion for health professions education would also apply.

title: Hubungan antara Literasi Digital dan Persepsi Mahasiswa tentang Etika Penggunaan AI di Kalangan Akademik
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational design with no control or comparison group, so the comparison and design criteria fail. The study also measures perceptions and digital literacy self-ratings rather than a learning outcome, and the domain is not clearly STEM. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order because there is no control group without generative AI. Under abstract-stage rules, the design evidence is positive, so exclusion is justified.

title: Percepción y usos de la IA en estudiantes del área computacional: un estudio descriptivo
rationale: Descriptive questionnaire study of 190 computer science students' uses and perceptions of generative AI. No control group and no comparison design; not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Outcomes are perceptions and usage, not a quantitative learning measure. Code E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order at abstract stage (no control group without generative AI), though E6 (non-empirical/descriptive survey) would also apply; the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy Among Teenagers and Its Association with Psychological Well-being: A Cross-Sectional Study Protocol
rationale: Cross-sectional study protocol measuring AI literacy and well-being; no learner interaction with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, no control group, and no intervention. Fails E1 in strict order, but the first applicable code is arguably E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) since there is no intervention at all. Study is also described as a simulated, non-empirical protocol with simulated participants, which points to E6. Per the code order, the first applicable code is E1; however, the record describes simulated data and a protocol, so E6 is the most defensible reading of the design. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-empirical design and absence of any generative AI intervention.

title: Enhancing human-AI communication in language education: Developing customized chatbots for teaching genre analysis and annotation
rationale: Abstract shows the content is English for Research Publication Purposes / genre analysis, a language-education topic rather than STEM, so E2 applies first. The study also reports chat histories and questionnaires with eleven doctoral students and no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would also likely apply, but E2 is the first code in order.

title: From lectures to learning outcomes: meaningful integration of AI-generated content in pre-clerkship medical training
rationale: Pre-clerkship medical training (genetics and pharmacology blocks) with LLM-generated summaries and flashcards. Medical education is a health professions context, which the protocol excludes from the domain criterion (health professions education is not STEM). Exclude at E2. Medical students are higher-education learners, so population is not the failing criterion. Design is unclear from the abstract (self-selected AI use with baseline comparison and difference-in-differences), but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion.

title: From computer-supported collaborative learning to human–AI collaboration: CSCL research in fifty years of Computers & Education
rationale: The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title indicates a review-style retrospective of CSCL research in a journal over fifty years ("CSCL research in fifty years of Computers & Education"), which is not an empirical study. This is positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so E6 applies. No quote is available since the abstract is absent.

title: Building foundations for independent clinical reasoning in an AI era: Student experiences with the independent authentic clinical reasoning task in prelicensure nursing education
rationale: The record is a prelicensure nursing education study on clinical reasoning. Nursing/health professions education is excluded from the STEM domain by protocol (Domain: exclude health professions education), so the record fails the domain criterion. No abstract is available, but the title alone gives positive evidence of a health professions context. Exclusion code E2 applies. Other criteria cannot be assessed from the title alone.

title: AI literacy: A core practice in world language education
Comparative Impact of ChatGPT and Conventional Search Tools on Clinical Reasoning Performance: A Randomized Crossover Study in Preclinical Medical Students [Letter]
rationale: The record is a letter to the editor commenting on a randomized crossover study, not an empirical study itself. It reports no original data for the authors' own experiment. The abstract text is a set of critical comments referring to the original study (n=46 preclinical medical students, ChatGPT vs conventional search, eight-point rubric). Under the protocol, a letter/commentary is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Publication type is also arguably not a journal research article, but E6 is the first applicable code in order. Population and the general topic appear to fit, but the record is not itself an eligible study. Note that the domain (clinical reasoning in medicine) may also raise E2 concerns, but E6 is reported as the first applicable code.

title: Birds of a feather: clustering mental models to explore how people think alike
rationale: Abstract describes a method that uses generative AI and network science to analyze students' textual mental models about ChatGPT, with validation against self-reported survey data. There is no learning intervention with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the study is a methods/elicitation study. Survey perceptions are not learning outcomes. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code in the order; E5 would also plausibly apply. Note that the first applicable code in order is E1 if the AI is not learner-facing, which is unclear here, so E3 is the best fit for the stated design.

title: The Analysis of the Misuse of the Quantifier “Ge”
rationale: The paper concerns the misuse of the Chinese quantifier "Ge" by international learners, a Chinese language topic rather than STEM. Protocol excludes language learning and other non-STEM content (E2), which is the first applicable code in order. The abstract also describes a conceptual/proposal paper with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, and ChatGPT is only mentioned as a suggestion, so further codes would apply, but E2 is the first that applies.

title: Analysis of Student Experience in Using Building Information Modeling (BIM) to Understand the Concept of Steel Structure
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study with thematic analysis of interviews with 10 students, with no separate control group. This is a qualitative design lacking a comparison group, which fails the comparison and design criteria. Although BIM is not clearly generative AI, the decisive failure is the absence of a control group (E3). Using the abstract-stage rule, exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison. Note that the rule to exclude only on positive evidence is met here, since the abstract explicitly states a qualitative approach and interviews only.

title: Designing a Digital Learning Ecosystem based on Gallery Walk with Virtual Board Technology
rationale: This is an editorial-style letter describing a faculty workshop built on Miro virtual boards and a Gallery Walk. It involves no generative AI as a learner-facing intervention (AI tools were only mentioned as used in article writing). The outcome is satisfaction and perceptions from 22 faculty participants, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code is E1, as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Participants are also faculty, not students. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because positive evidence of failure is present.

title: Research on Key Technologies of Adaptive Teaching Based on Student Digital Profiles—Student, Team, and Role Profiling Models for Process Evaluation in Project-Based Learning
rationale: Abstract describes a learning analytics/profiling framework for process evaluation of 165 students with no described control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome measured against a control. The design appears to be a descriptive system development study. Per the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is uncertain because the LLM generates teacher diagnostics rather than learner interaction, but the clearest failing criterion is the absence of a control group (E3). Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group.

title: WEBQUESTS AS AN INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGY FOR PROFESSIONALLY-ORIENTED FOREIGN LANGUAGE TEACHING
rationale: The study addresses professionally-oriented foreign language teaching (English for computer science). Content is foreign language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM. The abstract also gives no evidence of a control group or a quantitative learning outcome, and generative AI is only mentioned as a prospect. E2 is the first applicable code in order, so the record is excluded on domain.

title: Comparative analysis of multi-criteria decision making methods for prioritizing influential factors of ChatGPT adoption in higher education
rationale: The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title indicates a multi-criteria decision making study of influential factors of ChatGPT adoption, which points to adoption perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. The title gives positive evidence that the study prioritizes adoption factors via MCDM methods, not a controlled comparison measuring learning, so the outcome criterion appears to fail. Confidence is limited because the abstract is missing. Under the abstract-stage rule this should arguably be "unsure" rather than excluded, since the title alone does not fully establish the absence of a learning outcome.

title: Вплив діджиталізації на спектр вмінь англомовної компетентності студентів закладів вищої освіти в рамках професійної підготовки
rationale: The title (Ukrainian) and the supplied text concern English-language competence of university students, which is language learning and not STEM, so the domain criterion fails. The supplied "abstract" is actually a reference list with no study design, intervention, comparison, or outcome described. Domain failure is positive evidence, so exclude under E2. Note that the record also lacks any evidence of a generative AI intervention or a control group.

title: Artificial Intelligence Generators as Tools for Developing Academic Skills among University students
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of university students' frequency of use and perceptions of AI generators. It reports no randomized or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and usage only. Exclusion E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). The E3 comparison failure and survey design are also evident, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order is E3 for the missing control group; given the protocol's order, E3 would precede E5. Note: the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey without control group, so E3 is the first code that applies in order and should be used instead.

title: Transplantation & Tissue Engineering
rationale: The record is a withdrawn-titled, multi-abstract compilation from a transplant surgery journal's issue page (Journal of the American College of Surgeons). The abstracts concern transplant surgery, immunology, cost analysis, and survival outcomes in mice and patients. None describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool, and none concern STEM education. The record fails the intervention and domain criteria on the face of the text. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), which is checked before E2. The record would be E1 under strict code ordering, so the code should be read as E1 rather than E2. No quote is available because no passage refers to generative AI or learners.

title: AI-Enhanced Quality of Multimodal Physics Word Problems in Authentic Contexts Using the P-MAGIC App
rationale: Study is a physics (STEM) app using GPT-4o to generate problems, but the abstract reports evaluation of question quality by automatic and human (teacher) ratings. No quantitative learning outcome from students is described; "conceptual understanding" is asserted without a measured student outcome, and no control group is mentioned. Positive evidence of no learning outcome supports E5 at abstract stage. Note: the protocol's first-applicable ordering would place E1/E3 only if clearly shown; E5 is the clearest failing criterion here.

title: USE OF AI TOOLS IN DEVELOPING RESEARCH PROPOSALS AMONG PRE-SERVICE SCIENCE TEACHERS: A CASE STUDY
rationale: The abstract describes a case study with a mixed-methods questionnaire of pre-service science teachers using ChatGPT. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. The design is descriptive (case study, questionnaire), not an experiment or quasi-experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported (only usage patterns and perceptions). Per the protocol's exclusion code order, E1 does not apply because learners use ChatGPT directly, and E3 is the first failing criterion that applies on positive evidence. Exclusion is on the comparison/design basis, which is clear from the abstract.

title: Psychometric Properties and Assessment of Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice Towards ChatGPT in Pharmacy Practice and Education: a Study Protocol
rationale: Record is a study protocol for a knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) instrument about ChatGPT in pharmacy. No abstract is available. The title describes a psychometric/survey protocol, not an empirical controlled study with a learning outcome. Pharmacy practice is also a health professions domain, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion is on the basis of positive evidence from the title: it is a study protocol, not an empirical study, and it measures attitudes and practices rather than learning outcomes.

title: Making chemistry sing with AI
rationale: The record has only a title and venue (Nature Reviews Chemistry, 2026), with no abstract. The title and venue suggest a review-type article rather than an empirical study with a control group. Publication type is also a review-style venue, which the protocol excludes. Excluding under E6 (not an empirical study) because the record gives positive evidence of a review-style piece; no quote is available to support this beyond the title. Note that a reviewer may prefer to verify at full text, as the abstract is missing.

title: Mapping Challenges, Opportunities, Strategies, and Policies on the Use of ChatPGT in Indonesians Theological Higher Education
rationale: The abstract describes a literature study with descriptive analysis of challenges, opportunities, and policies. It is not an empirical study: there is no learner-facing intervention test, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Theological higher education is also not clearly STEM content. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first code that applies in the protocol's order given the literature-review design. Note that the protocol's order lists E1 first, but the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so E6 is the applicable code.

title: Changing conceptions of power: elites in Africa
rationale: The record is a conceptual/theoretical essay on elites in Africa (African Affairs). It is not an empirical study and has no generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the protocol's order is E1 (not learner-facing generative AI), so strictly the first code that applies is E1; however, the content is a non-empirical essay, and E1 would also apply since no AI intervention is present. Reporting E6 as the most fundamental failure is a judgement call; the audit should note that E1 is the first code in order that applies.

title: 生活支援技術習得におけるVR導入の現状と課題
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview-based analysis (content analysis of semi-structured interviews) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI use is only mentioned as LLM-assisted coding of transcripts by researchers, not as a learner-facing intervention, and the domain (care worker daily living support) is not clearly STEM. Fails design, comparison, and outcome criteria; not an empirical quantitative study, so E6 applies as the first failing code in order that is clearly evidenced. Note that E1 would apply first in strict ordering because the generative AI is not learner-facing; I am reporting E1 is the first code in order that applies.

title: Assessing AI-generated smoking cessation advice for patient education in primary care
rationale: The study evaluates AI-generated responses in a content-evaluation design. There are no learners interacting with AI, no comparison group, and no learning outcome; responses are rated by two specialists for readability, DISCERN, and accuracy. It is not an experimental study with a control group, so it fails on design, comparison, and outcome. Smoking cessation advice is also not a STEM domain and the population is patients, not students. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense) is the best fit for a rating study without learners, though the empirical label is debatable; the design and population failures are also clear.

title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY (LITERATURE REVEW)
rationale: The record is a literature review (self-described "Literature Review" in the title, and the methods are a PubMed data analysis), so it is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 applies. Its domain (clinical pharmacology, medicine) would also fall outside the STEM and student population criteria, but the first applicable code in order is E6 as the study is not empirical.

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption Practices in Scholarly Publishing of Early-Stage Academic Researchers
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey-style study of AI adoption and utilisation patterns among 50 graduate students and 50 faculty, analysed with descriptive statistics. It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports perceptions and usage. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison/design (no comparison group) and outcome (perceptions and usage only). Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is applied as the first failing criterion in order that is clearly evidenced; the E5 outcome failure is also present. Excluded at abstract stage on the basis of clear absence of a comparison group.

title: Shifts in economic discourse in online learning communities: evidence from the stack exchange
rationale: The title indicates a study of economic discourse on Stack Exchange online learning communities, which is not STEM content. No abstract is available. The title gives positive evidence that the domain criterion fails, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified under E2. No generative AI intervention, comparison, or outcome is indicated in the record.

title: A Eulogy for the Match
rationale: The record is a satirical/opinion piece (a "eulogy" for the National Resident Matching Program) in medical graduate education. The abstract mentions students using AI chatbots for application essays, but this is not a learning intervention with a control group.

title: A Case Study of ‘AI and Ethics’ on the Use of ChatGPT
rationale: The abstract describes a course case study of ChatGPT use with no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome; results are qualitative perceptions of advantages and disadvantages. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3 (no control group without generative AI). The course is a liberal arts elective, so STEM content is also unclear. Excluded at abstract stage on the clearest failing criterion.

title: Bilinear Sequence Regression: A Model for Learning from Long Sequences of High-Dimensional Tokens
rationale: Abstract describes a theoretical statistical-physics model (Bilinear Sequence Regression) with Bayes-optimal error computed analytically and a message-passing algorithm. It is not an empirical study of learners interacting with a generative AI tool, has no learner population, and reports no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first code that applies in an order-sensitive reading of the abstract; E1 would also plausibly apply since no learner-facing intervention exists. No positive evidence of an education context appears in the abstract.

title: Journal of Applied Informatics and Technology (Full Issue)
rationale: The record is a front-matter/full-issue table of contents for a journal issue, not a single empirical study. It is not an eligible journal article reporting an empirical study; it is a compiled issue listing. The closest match is publication type not eligible (E10). title: The Level of Children's Trust in Health Information Sources in the Lviv Region During Martial Law
rationale: Cross-sectional anonymous online survey measuring trust in health information sources. E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI); E1 is arguably also relevant since AI use is not an assigned learning intervention, but E3 is the first failing criterion for the comparison row as written. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by the explicit description of a survey design with descriptive statistics only.

title: Mathematics Student Teachers' Behavioural Intention Using ChatGPT
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire study using UTAUT to model behavioural intention to use ChatGPT, analysed by multiple linear regression. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome); the design is also a survey, not an experiment, which is a further failure, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order given the outcome is perception-only. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence that the outcome is intention rather than learning.

title: An AI-agent orchestrated real-time platform for peer-to-peer knowledge sharing
rationale: The abstract describes a system design/platform presentation with no evaluation, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It appears to be a system description rather than an empirical study, so it fails E6. No learning outcome is reported, which also argues against eligibility. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of absence of an empirical design.

title: Offline AI for Bridging Rural–Urban Educational Inequality in Central Asia: Insights from Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan
rationale: Abstract describes interviews and a survey of 153 students about access barriers and familiarity with AI tools. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is on E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first clearly applicable code; E5 and E6 also apply in substance since the study is a qualitative/survey study without learning outcomes. Positive evidence of a non-experimental design supports exclusion at the abstract stage.

title: Применение цифровых инструментов в системе подготовки учащихся 5-6 классов к математическим олимпиадам
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/methodological article discussing digital tools for olympiad preparation. It reports no comparison group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion under E6 (first applicable code in order is E1 possibly, but the abstract does not show a learner-facing generative AI intervention as an evaluated study; E6 is the clearest positive failure).

title: WORKSHOP DAN PELATIHAN PENGGUNAAN CHATGPT PADA PROSES PEMBELAJARAN DI SMA NAHDLATUL ULAMA PALEMBANG
rationale: This is a community service (pengabdian masyarakat) report on a ChatGPT training workshop at SMA/SMK schools. It describes delivering material and demonstrations, with no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning measure. The only result is a reported increase in understanding and skills, with no statistics. It is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies on the evidence available. Domain is Information Technology, which is not clearly STEM, but this is not needed as the first applicable code is E6 when the codes are checked in order. Final decision made at abstract stage on positive evidence of no control group and no quantitative outcome.

title: Digital Platform–Based Instructions and Adolescents’ Knowledge and Perception of Sexual-Risk Behaviour Consequences in Public Secondary Schools in Owerri Municipal, Nigeria
rationale: Content is sexual health education about sexual-risk behaviour consequences (HIV/AIDS, pregnancy, HPV), which is not a STEM domain under the protocol. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code. Also, the AI arm is described as "Meta AI/ChatGPT" without detail on the learner's generative interaction, but the domain failure is sufficient. Design is a quasi-experiment with a comparison group and the population is secondary students, so those criteria appear met.

title: Exploring the Experiences of Tertiary students in using Artificial Intelligence (AI)
rationale: Abstract describes a mixed-method survey and semi-structured interviews of tertiary students about their experiences using generative AI tools. There is no control or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported (only usage, challenges, and perceptions). Design is descriptive/survey/qualitative, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Per the ordering rule, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code. The E3 label is chosen because the absence of a comparison group is the first failing criterion; the design and outcome failures are also clear. STEM domain is not evident from the abstract. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-comparative survey/interview design, exclusion is justified.

title: Architectural Proposal for a Hybrid Recommender Engine for Accessible Educational Content
rationale: The abstract describes an architectural proposal validated through a functional prototype and a repository of documents, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence that the study is not an empirical comparative study (E6). Exclusion codes are applied in order; E1 is not clearly failed at abstract stage, so E6 is the cited code.

title: การจดการเรยนรตามแนวคดสะตมศกษารวมกบปญญาประดษฐเรอง การถายโอนความรอนเพอสงเสรมความคดสรางสรรคและนวตกรรมของนกศกษาระดบประกาศนยบตรวชาชพชนสง
rationale: The abstract describes a classroom action research design with 34 diploma students across three action cycles, with no separate control group that does not use generative AI. This is a single-group design, so it fails the comparison criterion (E3). The abstract gives positive evidence of no control group, so exclusion at abstract stage is warranted. Microsoft Copilot is a generative AI tool and the domain (heat transfer, STEAM) and population are acceptable, but the comparison requirement is clearly not met.

title: Exploring College Students' Utilization of Generative AI for Career Information Seeking: An Integrated Model with PLS-SEM and FsQCA Approach
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based (paper questionnaire) study using PLS-SEM and fsQCA on perceptions and intended utilization of GenAI for career information seeking. It is a correlational/survey design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcome is information-seeking behavior and perceptions. Per the protocol, survey designs are not eligible, and this is not an experimental study. Coded E6 (not an empirical study is the closest code, but the study is empirical). Note: the protocol's most accurate code for a survey/correlational design lacking a comparison group is E3 or E5; the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group and no learning outcome, so exclusion is clear. Using E5 as the first applicable code by order of evaluation would be more precise because no quantitative learning outcome is measured.

title: The Effectiveness of Publisher-Based Artificial Intelligence Models
rationale: Abstract is about drug dosage calculation instruction for nursing students. Dosage calculation is a mathematical skill, but the protocol's domain is science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, or data science, and health professions education is explicitly excluded. Nursing dosage calculation sits within health professions education, so the domain criterion is not met. The abstract also compares three AI tools without a clear non-AI control group, and reports no quantitative learning outcome, which would be further grounds for exclusion. Excluding on E2 as the first applicable code in the order given.

title: A project-based and AI-enhanced teaching framework for interaction design in digital media art education
rationale: Abstract stage, but the record gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design: it "proposes and implements" a teaching framework and says "By outlining practical workflows, this research offers a scalable and adaptable model." There is no comparison group, no control condition, and no reported learning outcome measure. Read as a framework/position paper with illustrative teaching cases, it is not an empirical comparative study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that the abstract stage rule normally requires positive evidence; the evidence here is that the abstract describes a framework with "teaching practice cases" and no comparison or outcome data, which supports E6, though a full-text check could still be warranted if the researcher disagrees.

title: Interacting with AI voice-based chatbots: A study on EFL students’ satisfaction and speaking performance
rationale: The study is a single-group pretest-posttest design with no control group, and the content is EFL speaking (language learning, not STEM).
